  - if continuing red-exit work, either make the labels truly causal with paired
    continuation outcomes or deploy them behind a narrow guard that only fires
    when exact/learned risk says follow-led will create a forced exit;
  - otherwise return to scaling strict causal-pair mining so red-switch positives
    come from survived counterfactual trajectories, not from deterministic
    switch-curriculum pressure alone.

## Run726 - 4p E1 m200 baseline ladder

- Goal:
  - follow `team_goal.md` E1 and replace 4p m10/m30 noise with a real m200
    same-policy survival ladder before doing more training.
- Evaluation:
  - full 4-player base game;
  - homogeneous same-policy tables;
  - `200` full matches per config = `800` hand rounds per config;

- Next:

    whether the gate needs evidence-based recalibration.

    evidence;

    it is low, the missing teacher must be table-wide/trajectory-causal rather

## Run728 - 4p E2 initial deal-floor audit

- Goal:
  - finish `team_goal.md` E2's intrinsic-floor check by estimating whether 4p
    deals are already negative-margin before any avoidable decision.
- Implementation:
  - added `quantum_cat_deal_floor_audit.py`;
  - samples fresh deals, advances chance to the discard phase, and computes
    each seat's exact own-hand liveness margin from
    `quantum_cat_liveness_oracle.py`;
  - reports both raw pre-discard margins and the margin after each seat's best
    legal discard.
- Definition:
  - `raw_negative_deal_rate`:
    fraction of deals where any seat has `margin < 0` before discard;
  - `best_discard_negative_deal_rate`:
    fraction of deals where any seat still has `margin < 0` after its best
    legal discard;
  - margin is the exact own-hand adversarial cell-deletion margin from
    `quantum_cat_liveness_oracle.py`.
- Verification:
  - smoke:
    `PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python quantum_cat_deal_floor_audit.py --players=4 --deals=20 --seed=20297071 --sample-limit=3 --out=az_runs/run727_4p_floor_m200_20260612/deal_floor_smoke_20_seed20297071.json`;
  - oracle tests:
    `PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m unittest quantum_cat_liveness_oracle_test.py`
    passed (`8` tests).
- Main 4p audit:
  - command:
    `PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python quantum_cat_deal_floor_audit.py --players=4 --deals=10000 --seed=20297081 --sample-limit=24 --out=az_runs/run727_4p_floor_m200_20260612/deal_floor_4p_deals10000_seed20297081.json`;
  - artifact SHA-256:
    `e50a08b3a7a4c6c011baa6a55a83b8008ce690d666c7f7e3fef90d0e61eef627`.
- Results:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Deals sampled | `10000` |
| Raw negative deals | `0 / 10000` |
| Raw negative deal rate | `0.00%`, Wilson 95% CI `[0.00%, 0.0384%]` |
| Best-discard negative deals | `0 / 10000` |
| Best-discard negative deal rate | `0.00%`, Wilson 95% CI `[0.00%, 0.0384%]` |
| Raw negative seats | `0 / 40000` |
| Best-discard negative seats | `0 / 40000` |
| Mean minimum raw seat margin | `2.8209` |
| 5th-percentile minimum raw seat margin | `2.0` |
| Median minimum raw seat margin | `3.0` |
| Mean minimum best-discard seat margin | `2.4980` |
| 5th-percentile minimum best-discard seat margin | `2.0` |
| Median minimum best-discard seat margin | `3.0` |

- Decision:
  - do not recalibrate the 4p `<40%` gate solely because of initial deal doom;
  - the sampled initial deals are not intrinsically negative-margin under the
    exact own-hand liveness oracle.
- Interpretation:
  - the 4p wall is not caused by unavoidable dead deals at setup;
  - the observed `67.50%..78.87%` m200 paradox rates are created by trajectory
    collapse after avoidable decisions, especially table-wide trick-6/7 exit
    allocation;
  - own-hand safety is still insufficient, because `oracle_safe` fails badly
    despite the initial own-hand margins being healthy.
- Next:
  - continue with table-wide/trajectory-causal labels or a table-protective
    teacher; do not spend more cycles on pure own-hand-safe teachers;
  - 5p E1 can run in parallel, but the 4p learning path needs causal
    continuation evidence for late table-wide exit allocation.

## Run729 - E4 web human-match JSONL logging

    on disk, so the human-Elo workstream no longer has zero collection

    `experiments/human_match_logs/web_human_matches.jsonl`;

    `--human-match-log PATH` and `--no-human-match-log`;
  - each completed game with at least one human seat writes one JSONL record;
  - added terminal-once protection so repeated `advance()`/snapshot calls do
    not duplicate completion rows;
  - added structured action history for human and bot decisions.
- Logged schema, version `1`:
  - source/session/timestamps:
    `source`, `sessionId`, `startedAt`, `completedAt`, `seed`;
  - table config:
    `players`, `humanCount`, `botCount`, `eligibleHumanVsBot`, `roles`;
  - bot identity:
    `botConfigSha256`, `botConfig.botMode`, `botConfig.botStatus`,
    `botConfig.bestCheckpoint`, `botConfig.bestCheckpointSha256`;
  - round/final outcome:
    returns, raw round scores, tricks won, predictions, discarded ranks,
    per-seat paradox flags, any-paradox flag;
  - public terminal state:
    completed tricks and final board ownership;
  - action history:
    actor, player, role, bot name, phase, trick number, led color, legal count,
    action id, and label.
- Test coverage:
  - added `quantum_cat_web_server_test.py`;
  - the test constructs a `GameSession` with `1` human and `1` heuristic bot,
    plays legal human moves until terminal, and verifies exactly one JSONL row
    with the expected schema fields.
- Verification:
  - `PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m unittest quantum_cat_web_server_test.py`
    passed (`1` test);
  - `PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m py_compile quantum_cat_web/server.py quantum_cat_web_server_test.py quantum_cat_deal_floor_audit.py`
    passed.
- Decision:
  - web human-game logging is now available;
  - no human-level claim yet, because no real human games have been recorded in
    the log;
  - iOS human-match logging remains undone.
- Next:
  - use the web UI to collect actual human-vs-bot games, or add matching iOS
    disk export so pass-and-play sessions feed the same Elo pool;
  - training-side next steps remain E3 4p one-cycle behavior distillation and
    E5 5p baseline ladder.

    verified wall is even higher.

    failure. It did not create avoidable off-led switches (`0` in both audits),

    Run730 `62.50%`), and the failure shape stayed identical: forced
    legal-count-1 paradoxes on trick 7.
- Next:
  - do not repeat this exact policy-stack guarded causal dose;
  - keep the strict Run730-distribution causal corpus as a diagnostic/data
    source;
  - the next 4p lever should either use the causal signal as a narrow
    deploy-time/hard guard for rare red-exit exceptions, or generate stronger
    table-wide continuation labels that score all legal alternatives by future
    exit allocation rather than one safe-vs-selected pair.

- Exact-pressure decision diagnostics:
  - m10 forced-only barely intervened (`5 / 1139` considered decisions) and
    got worse, so immediate forced-player reduction is too late/narrow;
  - m30 exact-pressure intervened much more (`1542 / 3533`, `43.65%`) and
    improved the same-seed screen by `10.83pp` versus public Run730 liveness;
  - exact-pressure m30 changed exact averages in the expected direction:
    forced players `0.0416 -> 0.0286`, min non-paradox legal count
    `9.3097 -> 9.6196`, total non-paradox legal count `42.8005 -> 43.3014`;
  - nevertheless it still failed badly at `52.50%`, and first paradoxes
    remained forced legal-count-1 collapses on trick 7 (`63 / 63`, led mostly
    red: `R=54`).
- Decision:
  - no promotion, no m200, and no pointer change;
  - reject a narrow immediate forced-only guard as a useful next lever;
  - keep broader exact legal-pressure as a teacher/label target, not as a
    deployed selector.
- Interpretation:
  - the current public liveness shield misses real table-wide pressure signal,
    because the oracle exact-pressure variant improves the same-seed m30 screen;
  - but even a hidden-information, all-legal exact-pressure selector remains
    far above the `<40%` gate, so a one-step hard guard is still not enough;
  - the next useful label family should score all legal alternatives by
    broader future exit allocation/continuation survival, rather than only
    immediate forced-player reduction or pairwise safe-vs-selected rows.

    led-token-loss/red-switch actions (`612 / 2400` token-loss top targets),

    existence of a good teacher.

  - either scale teacher-generated all-legal labels substantially with a
    held-out distribution check, distill a direct risk/Q head before policy
    cloning, or build an information-legal approximation of the table-liveness
    teacher as a selector;
  - preserve the Run735 teacher artifact as the current best 4p oracle label
    source.

  - Run736 relative q-policy did lower predicted selected risk versus the
    Run730 relative baseline (`0.1061` vs `0.1430` mean selected risk), but it
    still applied on almost every decision (`1125 / 1146`) and did not improve
    live survival enough;
  - threshold mode applied only `26` times but was worse (`77.50%`);
  - stacking q-policy under the public liveness shield made the m10 screen
    worse than same-seed Run730 liveness.
- Decision:
  - reject Run736 as a promotion candidate;
  - no m30/m200 continuation and no pointer change;
  - keep Run730 liveness shield as the best verified 4p information-legal
    config, and keep Run735 as the best oracle label source.
- Interpretation:
  - the table-liveness risk/value surface is learnable by the existing
    action-conditioned auxiliary stacks;
  - the current `q_policy` selector is the weak link: it is either too eager
    (relative mode), too sparse/late (threshold mode), or harmful when stacked
    under the public liveness shield;
  - direct risk/Q-head pretraining alone is therefore not enough at this scale.
- Next:
  - do not repeat this same aux-stack plus off-the-shelf `q_policy` selector
    route;
  - useful next transfer work needs selector calibration/abstention on
    on-policy live states, or a learned information-legal approximation of the
    table-liveness teacher's action ranking rather than raw q-policy dials;
  - a larger teacher-label corpus may still help, but only if paired with a
    held-out/live-distribution selector check so high replay correlation does
    not masquerade as survival progress.

## Run737 - 4p q-policy relative-dominance selector calibration

  - test the smallest plausible fix for Run736: keep the learned table-liveness
    action-value/action-risk stacks, but stop the `relative` q-policy selector
    from reranking almost every decision;
  - add a `relative_dominance` mode that only enters the lowest-risk safe set
    when the raw top policy action is at least
    `--action-paradox-min-risk-margin` riskier than the minimum-risk legal
    action.
- Source checkpoint:
  - `az_runs/run736_4p_table_liveness_aux_q_transfer_20260612/aux_stacks_s100_cpu/checkpoint_0000_loaded_replay_best.pt`;

    but records `rerank_relative_blocked_risk_margin` and returns the raw top

    `28 / 40 = 70.00%`, CI `[55.80%, 84.20%]`.
- Decision:
  - reject Run737 as a promotion candidate;
  - no m30/m200 continuation and no pointer change;
  - keep Run730 liveness shield as the best verified information-legal 4p
    config, and keep Run735 as the best oracle label source.
- Interpretation:
  - simple abstention disproves the narrow "relative failed only because it
    reranked too often" story;
  - throttling overrides from nearly every decision to `5.8-12.9%` still leaves
    m10 survival in the same failed `65-70%` band;
  - the bottleneck is therefore not just q-policy eagerness. The scalar
    risk/value heads can fit replay labels, but this selector does not turn
    them into good live action choices.
- Next:
  - stop spending runs on scalar q-policy knob sweeps for this checkpoint;
  - next useful transfer work should train an explicit information-legal
    approximation of the Run735 table-liveness teacher's action ranking, or
    collect larger live-distribution all-legal labels and validate a learned
    selector on held-out on-policy states before another m10 screen;
  - if using the aux heads again, treat them as features for a calibrated
    teacher-ranker/abstainer, not as standalone `risk` and `value` scalars in
    the current q-policy formula.

## Run738 - 4p table-liveness teacher-ranker graft failed low-coverage live screens

- Goal:
  - follow the Run737 conclusion by moving away from scalar q-policy knobs and
    training an explicit deployable teacher-ranker/abstainer;
  - approximate the hidden-info Run735 table-liveness teacher with
    information-legal pair features, then graft high-confidence candidate
    improvements onto the Run730 raw policy.
- Source/student checkpoint:
  - `az_runs/run730_4p_liveness_shield_behavior_distill_20260612/policy_stack_behavior_s100_lr5e5_cpu/checkpoint_0000_loaded_replay_best.pt`;
  - SHA-256:
    `163a1708a9ecf0edff585077fe90527a95289b868a6c369c74acbd24d6fafed5`.

  - SHA-256:
    `94194ece2d518c78d80fca534bcf625436c63e787a49902c06eb79e190ff17c7`.
- Implementation:
  - added `quantum_cat_table_liveness_improve_trainer.py`;
  - recomputes Run730 raw-policy anchors for each replay state, builds
    candidate-vs-anchor pair features using the existing deployable
    `ImproveMLP` feature schema, and labels a candidate positive when it
    improves table-liveness value by at least `0.08` without increasing
    table-liveness risk;
  - uses grouped state splits so candidates from the same state do not leak
    across train/validation.

- Interpretation:
  - the explicit teacher-ranker can learn a precise high-margin slice of the
    Run735 teacher labels, but the slice is too rare on live trajectories
    (`3.6-4.4%` override rate) to move same-policy survival;
  - lowering the threshold from `0.99` to `0.50` added only `10` overrides in
    the m10 screen and merely tied the same-seed public liveness control;
  - this is not a scalar q-policy problem anymore: a sparse pairwise abstainer
    still does not allocate enough table-wide exits across the whole round.
- Next:
  - do not repeat small high-margin pairwise `improve_graft` rankers from the
    same `2400`-row replay;
  - useful next transfer work needs broader/listwise supervision that changes
    many more live decisions while staying safe, or a larger on-policy
    table-liveness corpus explicitly balanced for the states where Run730
    enters trick-6/7 forced legal-count-1 collapse;
  - if using `improve_graft` again, train for calibrated coverage first, not
    only high offline precision.

    live same-policy play cares about decisive top-action changes, not just
    smoother mass over safe alternatives.
- Next:
  - retire soft/listwise policy-only CE optimization as the primary 4p transfer
    path, even with larger on-policy/late-balanced data;
  - next useful work should optimize the deployed top action directly:
    margin-based argmax/top-1 loss, DAgger-style live substitution with
    teacher-corrected states, or an information-legal teacher-approximation
    selector with explicit safe-coverage and false-positive gates;
  - if continuing policy distillation, make held-out deterministic
    table-liveness top-1 versus Run730 the offline gate before any live screen.

  - add a held-out discipline gate next to table-liveness top-1: follows-led
    rate, newly-loses-led-token rate, off-led token-loss rate, and red-switch
    rate versus the Run730 anchor.

    baseline;
  - keep Run735/Run740 labels as training-time diagnostics only.
- Interpretation:
  - the constrained filter helped relative to Run741: held-out red/off-led
    token loss is much lower than the unconstrained hard clone;
  - but it still moved too far from Run730's public-policy discipline: top-1
    improved by `+9.16pp` all and `+9.09pp` late versus Run730, while
    follows-led dropped `13.36pp` all and `6.34pp` late, and newly-loses-led
    rose `13.36pp` all and `6.33pp` late;
  - this exactly matches the Run741 warning: hidden-info table-liveness top
    actions can be correct with oracle knowledge but unsafe as an
    information-legal instinct;
  - `follow OR red-win-switch` is therefore not a strong enough constraint.
- Next:
  - add hard per-state action masks/penalties to the training target, not just
    row filtering: unless the action follows led, only allow red switches that
    are also high-confidence by a public proxy and do not newly lose a led
    token beyond a tight cap;
  - consider a two-head or gated objective: first preserve Run730's led-follow
    action unless the teacher improvement margin is large, then learn a narrow
    red rescue exception;
  - make the next offline gate explicit: beat Run730 on held-out
    table-liveness top-1 while staying within a small tolerance of Run730 on
    follows-led, newly-loses-led-token, off-led token-loss, and red-action rate.

## Run743 - anchor-preserving follow-led target fixed discipline but only tied live m30

- Goal:
  - move from Run742 row filtering to action-level constrained targets;
  - default to the Run730 public anchor action, and imitate the hidden-info
    table-liveness teacher only when the teacher action is safe enough;
  - first target: teacher follow-led corrections plus strict red rescue
    exceptions, with Run730-like discipline required before live screening.
- Code/infrastructure:
  - added `quantum_cat_constrained_policy_replay.py`;
  - the tool scores the Run730 anchor checkpoint on replay rows, then relabels
    each policy target as:
    - teacher action if it follows led;
    - teacher action if it is red, wins the trick, aligns with the prediction
      target, and beats the anchor by `red_rescue_q_margin`;
    - otherwise the Run730 anchor action;

  - reject Run743 as a promotion candidate;
  - do not continue to m200;

    baseline.
- Interpretation:
  - action-level anchoring solved the Run741/Run742 discipline drift:
    held-out follows-led and token-loss rates stayed essentially identical to
    Run730;
  - it also produced a small held-out top-1 gain over Run730
    (`+1.33pp` all, `+3.17pp` late);
  - live survival did not move enough: m10 looked promising because the control
    seed was awful, but m30 collapsed to a one-round tie
    (`60.83%` vs `61.67%`);
  - the learned raw policy remains worse than shielded play (`82.50%` at m10),
    so this did not move survival into the network.
- Next:
  - keep the action-level constrained relabeler; it is the first transfer path
    that preserves discipline while improving held-out top-1;
  - do not repeat this exact weak follow-led dose;
  - try a stronger but still disciplined variant: require teacher follow-led
    actions to have positive table-liveness margin over the anchor, and/or
    oversample only positive-margin follow corrections rather than training on
    all anchor rows;
  - the next live screen should require a clearer m30 gap before m200.

    Run743 already tied Run730 live m30.
- Decision:
  - reject Run744 as a promotion candidate;
  - keep Run730 liveness shield as the best verified information-legal 4p
    baseline;
  - keep Run735/Run740 table-liveness labels as training-time diagnostics only.
- Interpretation:
  - oversampling disciplined follow-led corrections did not reintroduce the
    Run741/742 failure mode: held-out led-follow and token-loss rates stayed
    Run730-like;
  - but it also did not produce a useful argmax transfer: `m001_rep3` was too
    weak, while `m000_rep3` moved all-play top-1 only `+0.17pp` over Run743 and
    lost `1.17pp` on late rows;
  - the current policy-stack-only KL-anchored recipe mostly shifts probability
    mass/CE under these anchored targets, not the deployed action enough to
    justify live screening.
- Next:
  - retire this positive-follow oversampling family at current scale;
  - the next 4p transfer should change the training mechanism, not merely row
    weights: examples include a larger unfrozen policy/head dose with a strict
    held-out discipline gate, a DAgger-style live substitution dataset where
    teacher corrections are collected from the student's actual mistakes, or a
    deployable selector trained for safe coverage instead of policy-stack
    imitation.

- Goal:
  - change mechanism after Run744 instead of retuning anchor-follow weights;
  - revisit `improve_graft`, but train and deploy it as a learned override on
    top of the current best public liveness base action rather than on top of
    the raw policy action;
  - accept only if a cheap offline gate found enough held-out safe override
    coverage to justify live m10/m30 screening.

  - reject Run745 as a promotion candidate;
  - no pointer changes;
  - keep Run730 liveness shield as the best verified information-legal 4p
    baseline.
- Interpretation:
  - the mechanism change is real and reusable: the trainer can now learn
    candidate-vs-public-liveness-base overrides, and deployment can compose an
    improve graft after the liveness shield;
  - the `48`-row cheap shard is underpowered for this selector objective:
    all-state metrics can look good while held-out validation sees only one or
    two overrides;
  - this does not falsify liveness-base grafting, but it does falsify tiny
    held-out screens as sufficient evidence.
- Next:
  - generate a larger liveness-base live-substitution corpus, probably
    `200-400+` rows, with grouped train/validation splits;
  - add or enforce an offline promotion rule requiring a minimum held-out
    override count, e.g. at least `8-10` validation overrides with high
    precision and safe rate, before any live m10/m30 screen;
  - keep the deployed `improve_base_mode=liveness_shield` path available for
    that larger safe-coverage attempt.

- Important negative detail:
  - the broad D640 model could produce `27 / 160` held-out overrides at a low
    threshold, but precision was only `0.148148` and mean value delta was
    negative (`-0.197411`);
  - stricter/lower-capacity models got precision but collapsed to `1-3`
    held-out overrides;
  - therefore the failure is not merely the old Run745 underpowered-validation
    problem.
- Live evaluation:
  - not run;
  - no candidate satisfied the explicit grouped held-out safe-coverage gate.
- Decision:
  - reject Run746 as a promotion candidate;
  - no pointer changes;
  - keep Run730 liveness shield as the best verified information-legal 4p
    baseline.
- Interpretation:
  - the liveness-base graft infrastructure is useful, and the new grouped gate
    worked exactly as intended;
  - scaling from `48` to `320/640` rows did not make this `ImproveMLP`
    selector generalize safe overrides;
  - all-state or training-set-looking coverage is actively misleading for this
    objective: broad thresholds accept many false positives, while strict
    thresholds abstain almost everywhere;
  - the next bottleneck is feature/objective quality for the selector, not just
    row count.
- Next:
  - do not keep scaling this exact `ImproveMLP` candidate-vs-liveness-base
    setup as-is;
  - mine the D320/D640 false positives and false negatives to identify which
    public tactical features are missing;
  - likely next mechanism: train a selector with explicit hard-negative
    mining/calibration on grouped held-out data, or add public table-exit
    pressure features to the candidate/base feature vector before another
    safe-coverage attempt.

  - the obvious public lane/exit signals are already represented in the audited
    snapshots: candidate/base/delta for follows-led, red choice, trick-win
    effect, off-led token loss, public slot damage, own/public exit damage, min
    open slots, min lane surplus, future token-loss pressure, and post-hit
    forced pressure;
  - D320 and D640 both show the same broad-selector failure: many selected
    overrides look superficially like rescues, but most are hard negatives;
  - the missed positives are not merely clean follow-led moves. Several are
    high-value, high-risk-reduction sacrifices such as red/off-led/trick-winning
    switches that newly lose the led token but reduce table-liveness risk by
    `1.0`;
  - therefore a simple additional rule like "only switch when red and winning"
    would be too blunt: it would capture some missed positives but still miss
    non-red sacrifices and would not by itself separate the false positives.
- Decision:
  - diagnostic only;
  - no live evaluation;
  - no pointer changes;
  - Run730 liveness shield remains the best verified information-legal 4p
    baseline.
- Interpretation:
  - Run746's failure is now better localized: the current selector has the
    important public pressure features available, but the pairwise
    `ImproveMLP`/threshold objective is not calibrated against hard negatives;
  - strict thresholds can be precise but abstain almost everywhere, while broad
    thresholds accept many false positives and miss many large-margin positives;
  - the next selector attempt should change the training objective/data
    weighting before adding another same-shaped corpus.
- Next:
  - train an explicitly contrastive/hard-negative-calibrated selector on the
    same grouped corpora before any new live screen;
  - include in-batch or per-state ranking losses that force the best positive
    action above same-state false-positive lookalikes, not just above random
    negatives;
  - oversample the large-margin missed-positive red/off-led rescue cases while
    retaining nearby false positives from the same state/group;
  - keep the grouped live-screen gate unchanged: at least `8-10` held-out safe
    positive overrides, high precision/safe rate, nonnegative mean value delta,
    and nonpositive mean risk delta before m10/m30.

### Run749 - legal-set selector with explicit abstain/base target still fails coverage

- Started: 2026-06-12 after Run748 retired the small independent
  candidate/base `ImproveMLP` liveness-base graft family.
- Goal:
  - test the first suggested architecture change from Run748;
  - make the shielded base action an explicit legal-set target, so the model
    learns "abstain/stay with base" in states without safe positive overrides;
  - score all labeled legal actions jointly with a learned set context instead
    of thresholding independent candidate/base pair logits;
  - only live-screen if the grouped held-out live-screen gate passes.
- Code/infrastructure:
  - added `quantum_cat_legal_set_selector_trainer.py`;
  - implemented `LegalSetSelector`, a DeepSets-style selector:
    - per-action MLP embedding;
    - learned mean/max set context over the full labeled legal set;
    - selection head over every legal action including the shielded base action;
    - auxiliary safe/unsafe head for risk-thresholded offline reports;
  - target construction:
    - if a safe positive override exists, target the best positive action;
    - otherwise target the base action, which means abstain;
  - evaluation:
    - choose the legal action with highest softmax probability;
    - override only if the chosen action is not base, crosses the probability
      threshold, and passes optional safe-prob threshold;
    - use the same grouped validation split and live-screen gate as Run746-748;
  - compile check passed:
    `PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m py_compile quantum_cat_legal_set_selector_trainer.py quantum_cat_table_liveness_improve_trainer.py quantum_cat_improve_graft_error_audit.py`.

    held-out gate.

  - reject the Run751 smoke selector as a promotion/live-screen candidate;
  - no pointer changes;

    baseline.
- Interpretation:
  - Run751 fixed the Run750 data-shape problem: same-state candidate labels now
    exist, q/risk labels cover candidate sets, and pairwise objectives can
    actually create state-local hard-negative pairs;
  - the existing failed selector's top proposal is usually not the right target
    (`7 / 8` primary proposals were negative), but the top-k candidate set often
    contains a better action (`4 / 8` target positives and candidate-set recall
    `1.0`);
  - candidate supply exists at tricks 5 and 6, but the first-eligible collection
    policy with `--max-states-per-match 1` collected only trick-4 rows; future
    late corpora need explicit trick quotas or per-trick collection passes;
  - the trainer still overfits/abstains at this scale, so Run751 is proof of
    infrastructure, not proof of survival improvement.
- Next:
  - scale this exact top-k shadow source to at least `128-256+` rows with grouped
    validation;
  - quota rows across tricks 4/5/6/7, or run separate trick-specific shards and
    merge them;
  - keep `proposal_audit_top_k >= 3` so pairwise/listwise objectives have real
    same-state hard negatives;
  - require the usual held-out override-count/precision/safe-rate gate before
    any m10/m30/m200 live screen.

- Live evaluation:
  - not run;
  - no selector variant passed the grouped offline live-screen gate.
- Decision:
  - reject all Run752 selector variants as live-screen/promotion candidates;
  - no pointer changes;
  - keep Run730 liveness shield as the best verified information-legal 4p
    baseline.
- Interpretation:
  - quota-balanced mining succeeded. We now have a reusable way to build
    late-trick top-k same-state hard-negative banks instead of accepting the
    traversal's first eligible trick-4 states;
  - trick 7 is mostly too late for the current failed-selector proposal source:
    only `1 / 32` target rows was positive;
  - the best selector did not fail by over-firing on trick 7: validation trick 7
    had `0` overrides. False positives came from earlier tricks, especially
    trick 4 and the tiny trick-6 validation slice;
  - trick 5 is close but not enough: `7 / 9 = 77.8%` precision at the best broad
    threshold, just under the `80%` precision bar, and that is still only a
    32-state validation split;
  - the current summary-feature `ImproveMLP` selector can now find coverage, but
    still cannot reliably separate early false-positive rescue lookalikes from
    real table-liveness improvements.
- Next:
  - do not live-screen Run752;
  - use the new per-trick diagnostics in all future selector reports;
  - next model work should be one of:
    - scale the quota bank to `256+` rows and validate whether trick-5 precision
      holds or improves;
    - add a trick-aware threshold/deployment gate after validation proves a
      specific trick stratum is precise enough;
    - add richer public features for early false-positive rescue lookalikes
      before another selector architecture sweep.

    live-screen gate by itself before any live match evaluation.

      filter for live-screen threshold diagnostics;

    close, but still misses the `>=80%` held-out precision bar by one false
    positive (`7 / 9 = 77.8%`);

    held-out trick-5 states;

    work is more trick-5 quota data and/or richer public features, not a live
    screen from a near-miss.

### Run759 - future led bottleneck audit attributes token-burn switches to earlier color/rank cell claims

- Date: 2026-06-12.
- Goal:
  - turn Run758's target into a causal diagnostic: for each future non-red-led
    switch where the target player still has the led token but has zero
    playable led-color actions, find the earlier decision that made that
    target player's potential action count in the led color drop to zero;
  - distinguish own-rank depletion from table-wide cell occupation by another
    player.
- Code changes:
  - added `quantum_cat_future_led_bottleneck_audit.py`;
  - the script plays homogeneous same-policy matches with a full neural
    selector payload through `load_neural_bots` + `make_eval_bot`;
  - for every future token-available/no-led-color switch that newly loses the
    led token, it scans prior decisions and computes the target player's
    potential legal count for that future led color before and after each
    action;
  - it records the direct zeroing cause when a prior action changes
    `potential_count > 0` to `0` while the target player's token remains
    available, plus the full chain of earlier count drops;
  - updated `.codex/skills/test-model/SKILL.md` to note that
    `quantum_cat_led_switch_audit.py` now supports full selector payloads.
- Input checkpoint:
  - `az_runs/run730_4p_liveness_shield_behavior_distill_20260612/policy_stack_behavior_s100_lr5e5_cpu/checkpoint_0000_loaded_replay_best.pt`.
- Recipe:
  - 4 players;
  - `40` full matches = `160` hand-rounds;
  - `match_context=true`;
  - seed `20260615`;
  - raw policy audit and liveness-shield audit on the same seed;
  - liveness mode:
    `liveness_shield?liveness_shield_base_mode=policy,liveness_shield_phases=play,liveness_shield_min_open_slot_delta=0,liveness_shield_min_public_damage_delta=0,liveness_shield_max_policy_log_gap=-1.0,liveness_shield_sample_limit=0`.
- Results:
  - raw policy:
    - artifact:
      `az_runs/run759_4p_future_led_bottleneck_audit_20260612/run730_raw_policy_m40_seed20260615.json`;
    - paradox context:
      `108 / 160 = 67.50%` hand-rounds with any paradox;
    - future token-available/no-led-color token-burn events:
      `205` (`1.2812` per hand-round);
    - direct zeroing cause found:
      `205 / 205 = 100.00%`;
    - total prior drop causes:
      `1250`, mean `6.0976` per event;
    - direct cause actor:
      `190` other-player / `15` same-player;
    - direct cause action in target led color:
      `204 / 205`;
    - target player had the direct-cause action rank in hand before the cause:
      `205 / 205`;
    - direct cause phase:
      all `205` in play.
  - liveness shield:
    - artifact:
      `az_runs/run759_4p_future_led_bottleneck_audit_20260612/run730_liveness_m40_seed20260615.json`;
    - paradox context:
      `99 / 160 = 61.88%` hand-rounds with any paradox;
    - future token-available/no-led-color token-burn events:
      `183` (`1.1438` per hand-round);
    - direct zeroing cause found:
      `183 / 183 = 100.00%`;
    - total prior drop causes:
      `1110`, mean `6.0656` per event;
    - direct cause actor:
      `160` other-player / `23` same-player;
    - direct cause action in target led color:
      `180 / 183`;
    - target player had the direct-cause action rank in hand before the cause:
      `183 / 183`;
    - direct cause phase:
      all `183` in play.
- Decision:
  - no promotion and no survival claim; this is an m40 behavior/causal audit,
    not an m200 gate;
  - keep Run730 liveness shield as the best verified information-legal 4p
    baseline.
- Interpretation:
  - this confirms Run758's "rank/cell/exit planning" diagnosis and makes it
    concrete: in the shielded run, almost all future token-burn bottlenecks are
    caused by an earlier play in the target led color and rank, usually by a
    different player, occupying the exact cell the target player later needed;
  - the label family should therefore be table-wide and opponent-aware: not
    only "preserve my led token," but "avoid claiming a color/rank cell that
    removes another player's last potential exit in that color when their token
    is still available";
  - this is still hidden-state/trajectory-derived training signal, not an
    inference-time feature. Deployment must learn it from information-legal
    observations/action features.

### Run760 - table-wide color/rank cell-exit protection labels

- Date: 2026-06-13.
- Goal:
  - turn the Run759 causal diagnosis into a training artifact;
  - label actions that would consume another player's last future exit in a
    still-tokened non-red color;
  - avoid recreating the Run741/742 over-red failure while still exposing dense
    per-action damage labels.
- Code changes:
  - added `quantum_cat_cell_exit_protection_miner.py`;
  - for each live play decision, the miner applies every legal action to a
    clone and counts target player/color pairs where potential future actions
    drop from `>0` to `0` while the target player's color token remains
    available;
  - saves standard replay rows with dense action-risk/action-value labels and a
    one-hot policy target;
  - after a smoke showed a naive "least non-red cell damage" policy target
    over-selected red, added `--anchor-policy-when-no-other-damage` and a
    follow-led-before-red tie-breaker. The final bank only changes the policy
    target when the deployed action itself damages another player's last exit.
- Input checkpoint:
  - `az_runs/run730_4p_liveness_shield_behavior_distill_20260612/policy_stack_behavior_s100_lr5e5_cpu/checkpoint_0000_loaded_replay_best.pt`
  - SHA-256:
    `163a1708a9ecf0edff585077fe90527a95289b868a6c369c74acbd24d6fafed5`.
- Recipe:
  - 4 players;
  - `40` full matches = `160` hand-rounds;
  - `match_context=true`;
  - seed `20260616`;
  - behavior policy:
    `bot_mode=liveness_policy`;
  - liveness knobs:
    `liveness_shield_phases=play`,
    `liveness_shield_min_open_slot_delta=0`,
    `liveness_shield_min_public_damage_delta=0`,
    `liveness_shield_max_policy_log_gap=-1.0`;
  - final replay:
    `az_runs/run760_4p_cell_exit_protection_labels_20260613/run730_liveness_cell_exit_anchored_m40_seed20260616.npz`;
  - metadata:
    `az_runs/run760_4p_cell_exit_protection_labels_20260613/run730_liveness_cell_exit_anchored_m40_seed20260616.npz.metadata.json`;
  - summary:
    `az_runs/run760_4p_cell_exit_protection_labels_20260613/run730_liveness_cell_exit_anchored_m40_seed20260616.npz.summary.json`.
- Results:
  - paradox context:
    `111 / 160 = 69.37%` hand-rounds with any paradox. This is context only;
    Run760 is a label-mining run, not an m200 survival gate;
  - decisions considered:
    `4543`;
  - rows collected:
    `1304`, or `8.15` rows per hand-round;
  - row collection rate:
    `1304 / 4543 = 28.70%`;
  - legal action damage signal:
    `1180` legal actions zeroed at least one other player's future color exit,
    with `1660` total other-player zeroed exits;
  - deployed selected-action damage:
    `647 / 1304 = 49.62%` collected rows had the deployed action zero another
    player's future exit;
  - policy-target changes:
    `647 / 1304 = 49.62%`;
  - final target safety:
    `1304 / 1304 = 100%` label-best actions had no other-player exit damage;
  - dense labels:
    each replay row labels all legal actions for both action-risk and
    action-value heads;
  - row trick distribution:
    trick `0`: `2`, trick `1`: `322`, trick `2`: `35`, trick `3`: `362`,
    trick `4`: `75`, trick `5`: `356`, trick `6`: `118`, trick `7`: `34`;
  - selected action colors:
    `Y:411`, `G:353`, `B:336`, `R:204`;
  - final label-best colors:
    `G:414`, `Y:400`, `R:347`, `B:143`;
  - changed-row label-best colors:
    `G:239`, `Y:226`, `R:143`, `B:39`.
- Decision:
  - no promotion and no survival claim;
  - keep Run730 liveness shield as the best verified information-legal 4p
    baseline;
  - use Run760 as the next training/evaluation input for a cell-exit auxiliary
    head or guarded policy-stack dose.
- Interpretation:
  - the label source is dense enough to train: almost one third of play
    decisions had a meaningful legal-action contrast;
  - the deployed Run730 liveness behavior often chooses an action that consumes
    somebody else's last exit (`647` rows), and every final label target avoids
    that other-player damage;
  - the anchoring guard is important. A naive least-damage policy target tended
    toward red because red never occupies non-red cells. The final target only
    moves the policy when the deployed action directly damages another
    player's exit, and prefers safe follow-led actions before red among ties.
- Verification:
  - compile check passed:
    `PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m py_compile quantum_cat_cell_exit_protection_miner.py quantum_cat_future_led_bottleneck_audit.py quantum_cat_led_switch_audit.py quantum_cat_full_match_elo.py`;
  - replay load check passed via `load_replay(..., return_metadata=True)`:
    `1304` rows, observation shape `(97,)`, action mask shape `(1000,)`, action
    features shape `(1000, 214)`, first-row policy sum `1.0`, and first-row
    risk/value labels on all `20` legal actions;
  - regenerated after the initial log entry so the replay metadata now embeds
    top-level `row_group_ids` for validation splitting: `1304` ids, `1304`

### Run761 - guarded policy-stack training from cell-exit labels

- Date: 2026-06-13.
- Goal:
  - test whether the anchored Run760 cell-exit labels can be distilled into the
    policy action stack without repeating the Run741/742 red/token-loss drift;
  - use grouped validation by the new `row_group_ids`;
  - reject before live evaluation if the policy argmax improves cell-exit
    damage only by sacrificing led-follow discipline.
- Input:
  - anchor/checkpoint:
    `az_runs/run730_4p_liveness_shield_behavior_distill_20260612/policy_stack_behavior_s100_lr5e5_cpu/checkpoint_0000_loaded_replay_best.pt`;
  - replay:
    `az_runs/run760_4p_cell_exit_protection_labels_20260613/run730_liveness_cell_exit_anchored_m40_seed20260616.npz`.
- Recipe:
  - `60` loaded-replay training steps on CPU;
  - train only policy action stack:
    `--train-policy-action-stack-only`;
  - policy CE plus hard ranking loss:
    `--policy-loss-weight=1.0`,
    `--policy-target-ranking-loss-weight=1.5`,
    `--policy-target-ranking-margin=0.75`;
  - anchor KL:
    `--anchor-kl-weight=0.05`;
  - validation:
    `25%`, grouped by `row_group_ids`, seed `20260617`;
  - output directory:
    `az_runs/run761_4p_cell_exit_policy_stack_20260613/policy_stack_s60_lr3e5_anchor005_cpu`.
- Trainer results:
  - frozen-parameter audit passed: `32` frozen parameter tensors, `0.0`
    max delta;
  - best snapshot by `policy_validation_top1` was step20:
    validation top-1 `45.71%`, CE `3.9627`, mean target prob `0.4036`;
  - anchor top-1 on the same validation split was higher at `47.24%`, so the
    trainer-selected best snapshot did not beat the Run730 anchor offline.
- Targeted cell-exit policy audit:
  - added `quantum_cat_cell_exit_policy_audit.py`;
  - audit artifact:
    `az_runs/run761_4p_cell_exit_policy_stack_20260613/cell_exit_policy_audit_all_doses_on_run760.json`;
  - Run730 raw policy on Run760 replay:
    target top-1 `48.24%`, other-exit damage `49.16%`, follows-led `92.25%`,
    newly-loses-led-token `1.30%`, red `15.87%`;
  - Run761 step20/best:
    target top-1 `47.47%`, other-exit damage `47.93%`, follows-led `91.41%`,
    newly-loses-led-token `2.15%`, red `17.33%`;
  - Run761 step40:
    target top-1 `47.01%`, other-exit damage `42.56%`, follows-led `82.59%`,
    newly-loses-led-token `10.97%`, red `26.07%`;
  - Run761 step60/final:
    target top-1 `49.00%`, other-exit damage `38.50%`, follows-led `76.99%`,
    newly-loses-led-token `16.56%`, red `28.30%`.
- Decision:
  - reject; no live screen and no promotion;
  - keep Run730 liveness shield as the best verified information-legal 4p
    baseline;
  - the late policy-stack doses learn the cell-exit label, but they do so by
    recreating the same discipline failure we have already seen: too much
    red/off-led/token-loss drift. The conservative step20 dose is too small and
    does not beat the anchor's target top-1.

### Run762 - separate aux-stack training from cell-exit labels

- Date: 2026-06-13.
- Goal:
  - keep the raw policy frozen and fit only separate per-action value/risk
    diagnostics from Run760;
  - test whether conservative q-policy selector knobs can use those aux heads
    to reduce other-player exit damage without policy-stack drift.
- Input:
  - checkpoint:
    `az_runs/run730_4p_liveness_shield_behavior_distill_20260612/policy_stack_behavior_s100_lr5e5_cpu/checkpoint_0000_loaded_replay_best.pt`;
  - replay:
    `az_runs/run760_4p_cell_exit_protection_labels_20260613/run730_liveness_cell_exit_anchored_m40_seed20260616.npz`.
- Recipe:
  - `80` loaded-replay training steps on CPU;
  - train only separate aux stacks:
    `--train-action-aux-stacks-only`,
    `--separate-action-value-encoder`,
    `--separate-action-paradox-encoder`;
  - reset the inherited aux heads:
    `--reset-action-value-head`,
    `--reset-action-paradox-head`;

    max delta;

    risk brier `0.1254`;

  - additive sweep artifact:
    `az_runs/run762_4p_cell_exit_aux_stacks_20260613/selector_sweep_run762_final_additive_on_run760.json`;

    other-exit damage `49.16%`, changed-row other-exit damage `98.92%`,
    follows-led `92.25%`, newly-loses-led-token `1.30%`;
  - best threshold/relative replay selector:
    other-exit damage `49.00%`, override rate `0.15-0.23%`, changed-row
    other-exit damage `98.61%`, unchanged-row other-exit damage `0.15%`;
  - best additive replay selector:
    other-exit damage `49.00%`, override rate `1.46-2.45%`, changed-row
    other-exit damage `97.54-97.84%`, but unchanged-row other-exit damage rose
    from `0.15%` to about `0.91-1.22%`.
- Decision:
  - reject; no live screen and no promotion;
  - Run762 learned useful-looking correlations, but the selector margins are
    not deployment-useful. Conservative threshold/relative modes almost never
    override; additive mode mostly trades tiny changed-row gains for new
    damage on rows the anchor already handled.
- Interpretation:
  - the Run760 label family is valid as a diagnostic, but this first policy
    stack and aux-stack transfer path is not enough;
  - next attempt should change the target shape rather than just train longer:
    for example direct shield-veto contrast labels, larger/repeated-seed cell
    exit labels, or a selector target that explicitly contrasts the anchor
    action against safe alternatives with a held-out precision gate.

### Run763 - trick-3 cell-exit improve-graft, then guarded lane-preserving deployment

- Date: 2026-06-13.
- Goal:
  - test whether Run760 cell-exit labels can produce a narrow deployable
    `improve_graft` selector on top of the current Run730 4p liveness shield;
  - use the newly available trick-gated validation/deployment path instead of
    repeating all-row grafts that had already failed;
  - after live samples showed the selector was burning led-color lanes, add an
    opt-in improve-graft guard that preserves the led lane unless an off-led
    red win is urgent for the acting player's bid.
- Code changes:
  - `quantum_cat_table_liveness_improve_trainer.py`:
    - fixed `_load_metadata_rows` so metadata JSON files that are plain lists
      load correctly, not only `{"rows": ...}` objects;
  - `quantum_cat_full_match_elo.py`:
    - added `improve_guard_led_follow`;
    - added `improve_guard_led_follow_red_win_must_be_urgent`;
    - added guard diagnostics:
      `improve_guard_led_follow_filtered`,
      `improve_guard_led_follow_base_follow_states`,
      `improve_guard_led_follow_responsible_red_kept`, and
      `improve_guard_led_follow_nonurgent_red_filtered`.
- Input:
  - checkpoint/base:
    `az_runs/run730_4p_liveness_shield_behavior_distill_20260612/policy_stack_behavior_s100_lr5e5_cpu/checkpoint_0000_loaded_replay_best.pt`;
  - replay:
    `az_runs/run760_4p_cell_exit_protection_labels_20260613/run730_liveness_cell_exit_anchored_m40_seed20260616.npz`;
  - metadata:
    `az_runs/run760_4p_cell_exit_protection_labels_20260613/run730_liveness_cell_exit_anchored_m40_seed20260616.npz.metadata.json`.
- Offline gates:
  - all-row gate failed despite a promising best held-out threshold:
    `129 / 316` overrides, positive precision `86.05%`, safe rate `90.70%`;
  - trick-3-only official gate passed:
    `42 / 78` held-out overrides, positive precision `92.86%`, safe rate
    `95.24%`, mean value delta `+1.4268`, mean risk delta `-0.7554`;
  - stricter threshold report also passed:
    threshold `0.9995`, risk threshold `0.5`, `37 / 78` held-out trick-3
    overrides, positive precision `100%`, safe rate `100%`.
- Live screens:

|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|

| Run763 trick-3 graft m10, threshold `0.99` | `az_runs/run763_4p_cell_exit_improve_graft_20260613/m10_run763_t3_improve_seed20260620.json` | `20260620` | `28 / 40` | `70.00%` | `47 / 160` | FAIL |
| Run763 trick-3 graft m10, threshold `0.9995` | `az_runs/run763_4p_cell_exit_improve_graft_20260613/m10_run763_t3_improve_strict09995_seed20260620.json` | `20260620` | `29 / 40` | `72.50%` | `44 / 160` | FAIL |
| Run763 guarded trick-3 graft m10 | `az_runs/run763_4p_cell_exit_improve_graft_20260613/m10_run763_t3_improve_guarded09995_seed20260620.json` | `20260620` | `22 / 40` | `55.00%` | `10 / 160` | noisy pass to m30 |
| Run730 liveness control m30 | `az_runs/run763_4p_cell_exit_improve_graft_20260613/m30_run730_liveness_control_seed20260622.json` | `20260622` | `76 / 120` | `63.33%` | n/a | control |

- Diagnosis:
  - the unguarded offline-passing selector failed live because it learned a
    replay-local improvement pattern that often overrode a led-color follow
    into an extremely low-policy-probability red play;
  - sample interventions showed led-yellow base follows being replaced by red
    plays with candidate policy probabilities around `1e-8` to `1e-5`;
  - the guarded selector filtered `3482` candidate actions in the m30,
    including `417` non-urgent red switches, and reduced live overrides to
    only `17 / 480` considered trick-3 decisions;
  - this made the graft safe enough to tie the control, but not strong enough
    to improve survival.
- Decision:
  - reject Run763 as a promotion;
  - keep Run730 liveness shield as the best verified information-legal 4p
    baseline (`481 / 800 = 60.12%`);
  - keep the new improve-graft led-follow guard as useful deployment/test
    infrastructure;
  - do not live-screen unguarded cell-exit improve-grafts again. Any future
    learned override on top of Run730 liveness should either train with
    lane-preservation/red-urgency constraints in the labels or deploy with this
    guard enabled from the first screen.

## Run764 - lane-shaped cell-exit improve-graft labels still tie live 4p control

- Date: 2026-06-13.
- Goal:
  - test the obvious fix from Run763: bake the led-lane preservation /
    urgent-red exception rule into the `improve_graft` training labels rather
    than depending only on a post-hoc deployment guard.
- Code changes:
  - `quantum_cat_table_liveness_improve_trainer.py` now supports
    `--force-led-lane-burn-negative`;
  - off-led candidates that newly burn the led-color token are forced negative
    when the base action follows led;
  - `--led-lane-red-exception=urgent_win` keeps only red switches that would
    win now, are not over-target, and either hit prediction now or leave the
    player needing all remaining tricks;
  - forced led-lane negatives are also forced unsafe for the auxiliary
    safe/risk head, and are reportable through `label_shape_counts`;
  - `--forced-led-lane-negative-weight` adds an extra hard-negative weight.
- Input:
  - checkpoint/base:
    `az_runs/run730_4p_liveness_shield_behavior_distill_20260612/policy_stack_behavior_s100_lr5e5_cpu/checkpoint_0000_loaded_replay_best.pt`;
  - replay:
    `az_runs/run760_4p_cell_exit_protection_labels_20260613/run730_liveness_cell_exit_anchored_m40_seed20260616.npz`;
  - metadata:
    `az_runs/run760_4p_cell_exit_protection_labels_20260613/run730_liveness_cell_exit_anchored_m40_seed20260616.npz.metadata.json`.
- Training recipe:
  - same as Run763's successful trick-3 offline gate:
    `bce_pairwise_margin`, metadata-group split, raw-summary observation
    features, `positive_value_margin=0.50`, `safe_risk_delta_max=-0.20`,
    `max_candidates_per_state=10`;
  - added
    `--force-led-lane-burn-negative --led-lane-red-exception urgent_win --forced-led-lane-negative-weight 2.0`.
- Label-shaping impact:
  - `1304` states, `9216` candidate examples;
  - class counts:
    `1379` POSITIVE, `86` NEAR_POSITIVE, `786` NEGATIVE,
    `6965` FORCED_LED_LANE_BURN_NEGATIVE;
  - `8793` candidates were in base-follow-led states;
  - `6965` candidates were forced led-lane negatives;
  - `3623` of those would have been raw positives;
  - `4822` raw-safe candidates were forced unsafe;
  - `1058` urgent red exceptions were kept.
- Offline gate:
  - artifact:
    `az_runs/run764_4p_lane_shaped_cell_exit_improve_20260613/improve_graft_lane_shaped_run760_t3.json`;
  - model:

- m30 Run764 diagnostics:
  - homogeneous gate eligible but failed: `84 / 120 = 70.00%`,
    CI `[61.8%, 78.2%]`;
  - first paradoxes were still almost entirely forced legal-count-1 failures:
    `83` at trick 7 and `1` at trick 6;
  - first-paradox led colors: `55` red, `12` green, `15` no led color,
    `2` yellow;
  - improve-graft candidates considered: `480`;
  - actual graft overrides: `28 / 480 = 5.83%`;
  - deployment guard filtered `3289` candidates, including `433` non-urgent
    red switches, and kept `0` responsible urgent red exceptions.
- All-play addendum:
  - all-row offline gate looked stronger than the trick-3 slice:
    threshold `0.9999`, `62 / 320` held-out overrides, `98.39%` precision,
    `98.39%` safe rate;
  - broad deployment still failed live m10 on a matched seed:
    Run764 all-play `27 / 40 = 67.50%` versus Run730 liveness control
    `26 / 40 = 65.00%`;
  - broader deployment fired more often (`50 / 1130 = 4.42%` considered play
    decisions) but remained far too sparse and slightly regressed survival.
- Diagnosis:
  - label shaping successfully removed the Run763 pathological off-led
    low-policy-probability red substitutions from the learned positive class;
  - however, after the strict live threshold and lane guard, the graft fires
    too rarely and too locally to change the downstream trick-6/7 collapse;
  - trick-3 candidate and same-seed control hit exactly `84 / 120`, and the
    broader all-play dial was worse than control at m10, so this is an
    infrastructure result, not a promotion candidate.
- Decision:
  - reject Run764 as a promotion;
  - keep Run730 liveness shield as the best verified information-legal 4p
    baseline (`481 / 800 = 60.12%`);
  - keep the trainer's forced led-lane-negative machinery as useful for future
    selectors;
  - do not repeat "Run760 trick-3 improve-graft plus stricter lane labels" as a
    standalone survival intervention. The next experiment needs broader
    trajectory/cell-exit credit assignment or a deployment mechanism that acts
    earlier/more often while retaining lane discipline.

## Run765 - handoff-pressure exact-exit graft overfires and regresses 4p survival

- Date: 2026-06-13.
- Goal:
  - test a broader trajectory-credit data source after Run764: mine decisions
    before the final forced-exit collapse, label every legal action by exact
    post-action non-paradox legal exits, and train an improve-graft that can
    make midgame pressure corrections on top of the Run730 liveness shield.
- Code changes:
  - `quantum_cat_table_liveness_improve_trainer.py` now supports
    `--base-action-source metadata_selected_action` and uses `row_group_id` /
    match-round-start metadata for grouped validation;
  - `quantum_cat_full_match_elo.py` now supports
    `improve_max_policy_log_gap` for `:improve_graft`, with
    `improve_policy_gap_filtered` diagnostics, so future grafts can reject
    candidate actions that are far outside the base policy's distribution.
- Input:
  - base/checkpoint:
    `az_runs/run730_4p_liveness_shield_behavior_distill_20260612/policy_stack_behavior_s100_lr5e5_cpu/checkpoint_0000_loaded_replay_best.pt`;
  - scaled handoff replay:
    `az_runs/run765_4p_handoff_pressure_20260613/handoff_pressure_m120_seed20260628.npz`;
  - metadata:
    `az_runs/run765_4p_handoff_pressure_20260613/handoff_pressure_m120_seed20260628.summary.json`.
- Mining result:
  - command asked for `120` matches but stopped at the `260` failure-round cap
    after `98` matches / `392` rounds;
  - `182` handoff-pressure rows, `1500` dense exact-pressure action labels;
  - warning tricks: trick 2 = `1`, trick 3 = `47`, trick 4 = `110`, trick 5 =
    `24`;
  - best-pressure actions were responsible red-win switches in `138 / 182`
    rows and lost the led token in the same `138 / 182` rows;
  - selected teacher actions never lost the led token in the smoke/scaled
    summaries, so this corpus specifically tests whether selective red
    pressure wins can beat pure lane preservation.
- Training result:
  - model:
    `az_runs/run765_4p_handoff_pressure_20260613/improve_graft_handoff_pressure_v1.pt`;
  - report:
    `az_runs/run765_4p_handoff_pressure_20260613/improve_graft_handoff_pressure_v1.json`;
  - `182` states, `1318` candidate examples;
  - classes: `723` POSITIVE, `85` NEAR_POSITIVE, `510` NEGATIVE;
  - objective: `bce_pairwise_margin`, grouped metadata split, raw-summary
    observation features, policy-context summary, base action from
    `selected_action`, `positive_value_margin=0.25`,
    `safe_risk_delta_max=-0.05`;
  - trick 3/4/5 held-out gate passed easily: at threshold `0.9999`,
    `42 / 46` validation warning states were overridden, with `100%` positive
    precision, `100%` safe rate, mean value delta `+1.0048`, mean risk delta
    `-0.5024`.
- Live screens:

| Config | Artifact | Seed | Rounds with paradox | Rate | Improve overrides / considered | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Run765 v1, no policy-gap guard, m10 | `az_runs/run765_4p_handoff_pressure_20260613/m10_run765_v1_guarded09999_seed20260629.json` | `20260629` | `30 / 40` | `75.00%` | `269 / 475` | clear overfire |
| Run765 v1, gap `4.0`, m10 | `az_runs/run765_4p_handoff_pressure_20260613/m10_run765_v1_gap4_guarded09999_seed20260629.json` | `20260629` | `26 / 40` | `65.00%` | `130 / 469` | improved but not enough |
| Run765 v1, gap `2.0`, m10 | `az_runs/run765_4p_handoff_pressure_20260613/m10_run765_v1_gap2_guarded09999_seed20260629.json` | `20260629` | `24 / 40` | `60.00%` | `107 / 468` | noisy pass to m30 |
| Run730 liveness control, m10 | `az_runs/run765_4p_handoff_pressure_20260613/m10_run730_liveness_control_seed20260629.json` | `20260629` | `25 / 40` | `62.50%` | n/a | matched control |
| Run765 v1, gap `2.0`, m30 | `az_runs/run765_4p_handoff_pressure_20260613/m30_run765_v1_gap2_guarded09999_seed20260630.json` | `20260630` | `84 / 120` | `70.00%` | `406 / 1430` | FAIL |
| Run730 liveness control, m30 | `az_runs/run765_4p_handoff_pressure_20260613/m30_run730_liveness_control_seed20260630.json` | `20260630` | `75 / 120` | `62.50%` | n/a | matched control |

- Diagnostics:
  - unguarded v1 overrode `269 / 475 = 56.6%` considered states at m10 and
    badly regressed survival;
  - adding `improve_max_policy_log_gap=4.0` filtered `634` candidates and cut
    m10 paradox rate from `75.0%` to `65.0%`;
  - tightening to gap `2.0` filtered `892` candidates at m10 and produced a
    noisy `60.0%` m10 result, but the m30 confirm regressed to `70.0%` versus
    `62.5%` for same-seed Run730;
  - the offline exact-pressure labels were therefore not sufficient: they
    identify actions that increase immediate exact legal-exit counts, but the
    learned graft still changes too many midgame decisions and can damage the
    longer trajectory.
- Decision:
  - reject Run765 as a promotion;
  - keep `improve_max_policy_log_gap` as useful infrastructure for future
    improve-grafts;
  - do not repeat dense handoff-pressure exact-exit improve-grafting as a
    standalone selector on top of Run730, even with `improve_guard_led_follow`
    and policy-gap caps;
  - next survival work should either train the base policy/aux heads directly
    from trajectory-level survival data or use a selector that includes explicit
    counterfactual continuation outcome labels for both the base and candidate,
    not just one-step exact exit pressure.
- Verification:
  - `PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m py_compile quantum_cat_full_match_elo.py`
    passed.

## Run766 - Run730 led-contrast continuation labels are clean but too sparse for graft transfer

- Date: 2026-06-13.
- Goal:
  - test the crossed follow-up after Run765: keep exact same-policy
    continuation labels for both base and candidate actions, but focus them on
    the user's central decision point: non-red led color, following led is
    legal, red switch is legal, and the current Run730 public-liveness base
    action follows led;
  - train an abstaining `improve_graft` on top of the Run730 liveness shield
    only if grouped held-out safe override coverage appears.
- Base checkpoint:
  - `az_runs/run730_4p_liveness_shield_behavior_distill_20260612/policy_stack_behavior_s100_lr5e5_cpu/checkpoint_0000_loaded_replay_best.pt`;
  - SHA-256:
    `163a1708a9ecf0edff585077fe90527a95289b868a6c369c74acbd24d6fafed5`;
  - collection mode: `liveness_policy`, play-only liveness shield,
    `min_open_slot_delta=0`, `min_public_damage_delta=0`, policy gap `-1.0`.
- Operational note:
  - an initial broader `legal<=14`, `max_decisions=180` generation was
    interrupted after repeated long full-continuation branches and no artifact
    was written;
  - the finished diagnostic therefore capped legal count at `8` and evaluated
    trick `3-5` led-contrast positions only.
- Smoke corpus:
  - artifact:
    `az_runs/run766_4p_run730_led_contrast_graft_20260613/led_contrast_liveness_t3_t5_legal8_d32_seed20260632.npz`;
  - evaluated decisions: `32`;
  - retained exact-continuation contrast rows: `14`;
  - skipped no-action-paradox-contrast rows: `18`;
  - all `32` evaluated base actions were `selected_follow_led`;
  - label-best actions: `10 / 14` followed led, `2 / 14` were red switches,
    and `2 / 14` were other switches.
- Scaled diagnostic corpus:
  - artifact:
    `az_runs/run766_4p_run730_led_contrast_graft_20260613/led_contrast_liveness_t3_t5_legal8_d96_seed20260633.npz`;
  - source simulation: `130` rounds, `76` source paradox rounds;
  - evaluated decisions: `96`;
  - retained exact-continuation contrast rows: `59`;
  - skipped no-action-paradox-contrast rows: `37`;
  - all `96` evaluated base actions were `selected_follow_led`;
  - dense policy target changed on `39 / 59` retained rows;
  - baseline selected action led to any-player paradox on `17 / 59` retained
    rows and actor paradox on `3 / 59`;
  - retained trick distribution: trick 3 = `9`, trick 4 = `45`, trick 5 = `5`;
  - label-best colors: green `39`, red `14`, yellow `6`;
  - label-best follow-led split: `44 / 59` follow-led, `14 / 59` red switch,
    `1 / 59` other;
  - continuation outcome safety rates by action bucket:
    - red switches: `47 / 220 = 21.4%` safe;
    - green follow-led actions: `106 / 162 = 65.4%` safe;
    - yellow follow-led actions: `9 / 15 = 60.0%` safe.
- Rank-allocation diagnostic:
  - label-best rank minus base rank averaged `+0.59`;
  - for follow-led targets, mean rank delta was `+0.66`;
  - the most common delta was still `0`, so the signal is not simply
    "always play higher," but the examples often replace the base led-color
    card with a higher or different led-color card.
- Training:
  - model:
    `az_runs/run766_4p_run730_led_contrast_graft_20260613/improve_led_contrast_d59_v1.pt`;
  - report:
    `az_runs/run766_4p_run730_led_contrast_graft_20260613/improve_led_contrast_d59_v1.json`;
  - `59` states, `365` candidate examples;
  - class counts: `43` POSITIVE, `3` NEAR_POSITIVE, `319` NEGATIVE;
  - grouped metadata split: `44` train groups / `15` validation groups;
  - objective: `bce_pairwise_margin`, raw-summary observation features,
    policy-context summary, `base_action_source=metadata_policy_best`;
  - all-state threshold report looked good at low thresholds:
    `13 / 59` overrides, `100%` precision/safe rate, mean value delta
    `+1.7282`, mean risk delta `-1.0`.
- Offline gate:
  - predeclared live gate required at least `4` grouped held-out overrides,
    precision `>=90%`, safe rate `>=90%`, mean value delta `>=0.25`, and mean
    risk delta `<=-0.05`;
  - best grouped validation threshold found only `1 / 15` held-out override,
    even though that one was positive and safe;
  - `live_screen_gate.passed=false`, so no live m10/m30 screen was run.
- Decision:
  - reject Run766 as a promotion/live-screen candidate;
  - keep Run730 liveness shield as the best verified information-legal 4p
    baseline;
  - keep this corpus shape as diagnostic evidence, not deployment evidence.
- Interpretation:
  - this is the cleanest current-Run730 evidence that "red when switching" is
    not the main survival correction in the non-red-led/follow-legal slice;
  - in these exact continuation labels, red switches are often unsafe, while
    the label-best action usually remains in the led color and often changes
    rank/card choice inside that lane;
  - the next useful curriculum should target led-color rank/exit allocation
    under same-policy continuation, with enough grouped data to validate
    coverage, rather than another small `ImproveMLP` graft or another broad
    red-switch selector.
- Verification:
  - `PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m py_compile quantum_cat_live_substitution_replay.py quantum_cat_table_liveness_improve_trainer.py quantum_cat_full_match_elo.py`
    passed.

## Run767 - Larger led-rank continuation corpus confirms the signal but still fails held-out selector transfer

- Date: 2026-06-13.
- Goal:
  - continue the Run766 non-red-led/follow-legal slice, but scale it enough to
    test whether the missing skill is led-color rank/exit allocation rather
    than red switching;
  - preserve live-substitution sidecar metadata through replay mixing so the
    trainer can use the deployed base action via
    `base_action_source=metadata_policy_best`;
  - train only offline candidates first, and live-screen only if grouped
    held-out safe override coverage passes the predeclared gate.
- Infrastructure:
  - added `--sidecar-metadata-out` to
    `quantum_cat_weighted_replay_mix.py`;
  - smoke-merged Run766 d32+d96 into `73` rows and verified `73` sidecar rows
    in the same sampled/shuffled order.
- Base checkpoint:
  - `az_runs/run730_4p_liveness_shield_behavior_distill_20260612/policy_stack_behavior_s100_lr5e5_cpu/checkpoint_0000_loaded_replay_best.pt`;
  - SHA-256:
    `163a1708a9ecf0edff585077fe90527a95289b868a6c369c74acbd24d6fafed5`;
  - collection mode: `liveness_policy`, play-only liveness shield,
    `min_open_slot_delta=0`, `min_public_damage_delta=0`, policy gap `-1.0`.
- New continuation shards:
  - seed `20260641`: `96` evaluated decisions, `55` retained contrast rows,
    `40 / 55` dense target changes, baseline any-player paradox `19 / 55`,
    actor paradox `8 / 55`;
  - seed `20260642`: `96` evaluated decisions, `54` retained contrast rows,
    `38 / 54` dense target changes, baseline any-player paradox `20 / 54`,
    actor paradox `5 / 54`.
- Merged corpus:
  - artifact:
    `az_runs/run767_4p_led_rank_allocation_20260613/led_rank_liveness_merged_d182_seed20260640.npz`;
  - sources: Run766 d32 = `14` rows, Run766 d96 = `59` rows, seed41 = `55`
    rows, seed42 = `54` rows;
  - total rows: `182`;
  - grouped split used by training: `110` groups, `82` train groups,
    `28` validation groups; `135` train states, `47` validation states;
  - trick distribution: trick 3 = `32`, trick 4 = `142`, trick 5 = `8`;
  - led colors: green `149`, yellow `33`.
- Data finding:
  - the deployed base action followed led in all `182 / 182` retained rows;
  - label-best action changed on `127 / 182 = 69.8%` rows;
  - label-best split: `131 / 182` follow-led, `41 / 182` red switch,
    `10 / 182` other switch;
  - base action continuation paradox: any-player `60 / 182 = 33.0%`,
    actor `17 / 182 = 9.3%`;
  - label-best continuation paradox: any-player `0 / 182`, actor `0 / 182`;
  - candidate continuation safety by bucket:
    - follow-led: `62.8%` safe (`537` candidates);
    - red switch: `20.6%` safe (`698` candidates);
    - other switch: `42.4%` safe (`99` candidates);
  - when `would_win_now` was observable, red switches won `125 / 125 = 100%`,
    but that did not make them survival-safe;
  - label-best rank minus base rank averaged `+0.48`; for follow-led
    label-best actions it averaged `+0.69`, but the mode was still `0`, so the
    target is "choose the right led-lane exit card," not "always play higher."
- Training v1:
  - model:
    `az_runs/run767_4p_led_rank_allocation_20260613/improve_led_rank_d182_v1.pt`;
  - report:
    `az_runs/run767_4p_led_rank_allocation_20260613/improve_led_rank_d182_v1.json`;
  - objective: `bce_pairwise_margin`, raw-summary observation features,
    policy-context summary, `base_action_source=metadata_policy_best`;
  - class counts: `133` POSITIVE, `25` NEAR_POSITIVE, `994` NEGATIVE;
  - all-state thresholds looked tempting, but the grouped validation best was
    only `4 / 47` overrides at `50%` positive precision/safe rate;
  - `live_screen_gate.passed=false`.
- Training v2 precision:
  - model:
    `az_runs/run767_4p_led_rank_allocation_20260613/improve_led_rank_d182_v2_precision.pt`;
  - report:
    `az_runs/run767_4p_led_rank_allocation_20260613/improve_led_rank_d182_v2_precision.json`;
  - changes: smaller/regularized model, no positive class balancing, stronger
    false-positive penalty, `--force-led-lane-burn-negative`,
    `--led-lane-red-exception urgent_win`, and
    `--forced-led-lane-negative-weight 3.0`;
  - shaped class counts: `84` POSITIVE, `8` NEAR_POSITIVE, `325` NEGATIVE,
    `735` FORCED_LED_LANE_BURN_NEGATIVE;
  - label shaping forced `49` raw-positive off-led lane-burn candidates
    negative and kept `62` urgent-red exceptions;
  - all-state precision became high but coverage collapsed;
  - grouped validation best made `0 / 47` overrides;
  - `live_screen_gate.passed=false`.
- Decision:
  - reject Run767 as a live-screen or promotion candidate;
  - keep Run730 liveness shield as the best verified 4p survival baseline;
  - keep the merged d182 corpus and sidecar-preserving mixer as useful
    infrastructure/evidence.
- Interpretation:
  - Run767 strengthens the Run766 conclusion: red is not the missing primary
    behavior in this slice, even though red switches win the trick when the
    win is observable;
  - the model needs a representation/training target that generalizes
    table-wide led-lane rank/exit allocation across groups, not another small
    independent `ImproveMLP` threshold sweep;
  - next best attempt should use a stronger action-conditioned/legal-set model
    or trajectory-level/table-wide survival targets over this exact
    continuation data, with grouped validation kept as the promotion gate.
- Verification:
  - `PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m py_compile quantum_cat_weighted_replay_mix.py`
    passed;
  - smoke sidecar merge check returned
    `{'npz_rows': 73, 'sidecar_rows': 73, 'match': True}`.

## Run768 - Legal-set selector learns the d182 corpus but still fails grouped held-out coverage

- Date: 2026-06-13.
- Goal:
  - follow the Run767 decision and test a stronger set-aware/action-conditioned
    model on the exact d182 led-rank continuation corpus instead of another
    independent `ImproveMLP` threshold sweep;
  - keep the same grouped validation gate and do no live screen unless the
    offline safe-coverage gate passes.
- Corpus:
  - replay:
    `az_runs/run767_4p_led_rank_allocation_20260613/led_rank_liveness_merged_d182_seed20260640.npz`;
  - sidecar:
    `az_runs/run767_4p_led_rank_allocation_20260613/led_rank_liveness_merged_d182_seed20260640.npz.metadata.json`;
  - total states: `182`, legal action rows: `1334`;
  - grouped split: `110` groups, `82` train groups, `28` validation groups;
    `134` train states and `48` validation states under seed `20299321`.
- Infrastructure:
  - `quantum_cat_legal_set_selector_trainer.py` already trained a DeepSets-style
    `LegalSetSelector`, but had no led-lane label shaping;
  - added `--force-led-lane-burn-negative` and
    `--led-lane-red-exception {none,win,urgent_win}` to mirror the
    `ImproveMLP` trainer's feature-level led-lane rule.
- v1 legal-set model:
  - model:
    `az_runs/run768_4p_led_rank_legal_set_20260613/legal_set_led_rank_d182_v1.pt`;
  - report:
    `az_runs/run768_4p_led_rank_legal_set_20260613/legal_set_led_rank_d182_v1.json`;
  - setup: hidden `128`, `220` epochs, target mode
    `best_positive_else_base`, positive weight `1.5`, safe loss weight `0.5`;
  - train/all-row fit was strong, but grouped validation best was only
    `2 / 48` overrides at `100%` precision/safe rate;
  - thresholds with at least `8` validation overrides topped out at about
    `55.6%` precision/safe rate;
  - `live_screen_gate.passed=false`.
- v2 small/early-stopped model:
  - model:
    `az_runs/run768_4p_led_rank_legal_set_20260613/legal_set_led_rank_d182_v2_small.pt`;
  - report:
    `az_runs/run768_4p_led_rank_legal_set_20260613/legal_set_led_rank_d182_v2_small.json`;
  - setup: hidden `32`, `55` epochs, target mode
    `best_value_positive_else_base`, no positive upweight, safe loss weight
    `1.0`;
  - grouped validation best was `4 / 48` overrides at `50%`
    precision/safe rate;
  - `live_screen_gate.passed=false`.
- v3 led-lane-shaped legal-set model:
  - model:
    `az_runs/run768_4p_led_rank_legal_set_20260613/legal_set_led_rank_d182_v3_ledshape.pt`;
  - report:
    `az_runs/run768_4p_led_rank_legal_set_20260613/legal_set_led_rank_d182_v3_ledshape.json`;
  - setup: hidden `64`, `140` epochs, target mode
    `best_positive_else_base`, positive weight `1.2`, safe loss weight `0.75`,
    `--force-led-lane-burn-negative`,
    `--led-lane-red-exception urgent_win`;
  - label shaping counts:
    - `735` forced led-lane-burn negatives;
    - `49` raw-positive off-led burns forced negative/unsafe;
    - `62` urgent red-win exceptions kept;
  - all-row thresholds again looked strong, but grouped validation best was
    still only `2 / 48` overrides at `100%` precision/safe rate;
  - `live_screen_gate.passed=false`.
- Decision:
  - reject all Run768 candidates as live-screen or promotion candidates;
  - keep the legal-set led-lane shaping patch as useful infrastructure;
  - no live m10/m30 screen was run.
- Interpretation:
  - a set-aware architecture helps fit the corpus and the led-lane rule cleans
    up labels, but d182 is still not enough for reliable grouped
    generalization;
  - the immediate next step should be more trajectory-diverse continuation
    data or cross-validated/source-balanced training before deployer support
    for `LegalSetSelector` is worth adding;
  - the legal-set trainer is also slow for this tiny corpus, so vectorizing the
    per-state loop would be useful if we scale this path.
- Verification:

## Run769 - Broader led-continuation replay increases diversity but still fails grouped selector transfer

- Date: 2026-06-13.
- Goal:
  - follow Run768's conclusion by changing the data source rather than
    continuing architecture/threshold sweeps on the same `182` rows;
  - broaden the led-contrast continuation slice from trick `3-5`, legal count
    `<=8`, follow-led-only behavior into trick `2-5`, legal count `<=10`, and
    an exploration shard that includes selected off-led switches;
  - keep the strict grouped offline live-screen gate before any live m10/m30
    evaluation.
- Base checkpoint:
  - `az_runs/run730_4p_liveness_shield_behavior_distill_20260612/policy_stack_behavior_s100_lr5e5_cpu/checkpoint_0000_loaded_replay_best.pt`;
  - collection mode: `liveness_policy`, play-only liveness shield,
    `min_open_slot_delta=0`, `min_public_damage_delta=0`, policy gap `-1.0`.
- New continuation shards:

    `96` evaluated decisions, `64` retained rows, selected bucket
    `64 / 64` follow-led, baseline any-player paradox `30 / 64`;
  - exploration broader shard:
    `az_runs/run769_4p_broader_led_continuation_20260613/led_broader_explore_t2_t5_legal10_d96_seed20260652.npz`;
    `96` evaluated decisions, `40` retained rows, selected bucket split
    `26` follow-led, `13` non-red switch, `1` red switch; baseline any-player
    paradox `20 / 40`.
- Merged corpora:
  - append corpus:
    `az_runs/run769_4p_broader_led_continuation_20260613/led_broader_append_d286_seed20260653.npz`;
    `286` rows, `286` groups, no replacement; sources: Run767 d182 = `182`,
    Run769 on-policy = `64`, Run769 exploration = `40`;
  - balanced corpus:
    `az_runs/run769_4p_broader_led_continuation_20260613/led_broader_balanced_d264_seed20260654.npz`;
    `264` rows, `217` row groups in the mix summary; sources: Run767 d182 =

    diagnostic rather than `80` independent exploration rows;
  - sidecar alignment verified: append `286 / 286`, balanced `264 / 264`.
- Data findings:
  - append corpus:
    - deployed base action buckets: `272` follow-led, `13` other switch,
      `1` red switch;
    - label-best buckets: `195` follow-led, `54` red switch, `37` other
      switch;
    - policy target changed on `205 / 286 = 71.7%` rows;
    - base continuation any-player paradox: `110 / 286 = 38.5%`;
      label-best continuation any-player paradox: `0 / 286`;
    - candidate continuation safety by bucket: follow-led `506 / 849 = 59.6%`,
      red switch `211 / 937 = 22.5%`, other switch `188 / 446 = 42.2%`;
  - balanced corpus:
    - deployed base action buckets: `237` follow-led, `26` other switch,
      `1` red switch;
    - label-best buckets: `164` follow-led, `44` red switch, `56` other
      switch;
    - policy target changed on `188 / 264 = 71.2%` rows;
    - base continuation any-player paradox: `109 / 264 = 41.3%`;
      label-best continuation any-player paradox: `0 / 264`;
    - candidate continuation safety by bucket: follow-led `443 / 788 = 56.2%`,
      red switch `168 / 700 = 24.0%`, other switch `283 / 617 = 45.9%`;
  - red-switch label-best actions with observable `would_win_now` still won
    `100%` of known cases in both corpora, but red-switch candidates remained
    much less survival-safe than follow-led candidates overall.
- Balanced legal-set model:
  - model:
    `az_runs/run769_4p_broader_led_continuation_20260613/legal_set_broader_balanced_d264_v1_ledshape.pt`;
  - report:
