### Run971 - best-of-N/RFT applies here, but hard-negative source collection needed no-exclude candidates

- Date: `2026-06-15`.
- Question:
  - Is the modern LLM "Strawberry-style" idea applicable here: run multiple
    candidate continuations, score or filter them, then make the better moves a
    little more likely?
  - If yes, have we already tried it, and what is currently blocking transfer?
- Research framing:
  - OpenAI's o1 note describes improved reasoning from train-time
    reinforcement learning plus more test-time compute/search;
  - ReST generates samples from the current policy, filters/scores them, and
    improves the model offline from the selected data;
  - STaR keeps successful self-generated reasoning traces and fine-tunes on
    them;
  - GRPO-style reasoning RL scores multiple samples for the same prompt and
    updates from their relative advantage;
  - the Cat-in-the-Box analogue is expert iteration / rejection-sampling
    fine-tuning over game states: for one state, score several legal
    actions/continuations, then train the policy or verifier toward the better
    actions.
- Repo evidence before this run:
  - Run946 implemented the literal small policy nudge:
    alpha-`0.35` blended repeat-validated best-of-N targets into the base
    policy. It moved target probabilities offline but did not improve live
    same-policy survival;
  - Run947 made the best-of-N target top-1 on every transformed row and moved
    held-out target probabilities, but live smokes still failed the `<40%`
    paradox-round gate;
  - Run948 scaled to `34` rows from `12` sources and still worsened live
    survival;
  - Run949 moved the same idea into a proposal reranker. Saved-slate top-1 was
    nearly perfect, but live same-policy survival still failed because
    on-policy false positives were not represented well enough.
- Code change:
  - `quantum_cat_live_substitution_replay.py` now applies the
    `bad_red_no_win_and_lane_preserver` shape as a cheap raw legal-set
    preproposal filter before expensive action-set feature scoring;
  - the action-set transformer proposal path now reruns that same shape against
    the true base action before scoring candidates;
  - the proposal call now receives the collection summary so these counters are
    visible;
  - this keeps the modern best-of-N/RFT loop, but directs compute at the user's
    actual hard case: red off-led lane burns that do not win when a
    lane-preserving alternative exists.
- New collection evidence:
  - cap-`16` MPS smoke with the default forced-lane-negative exclusion still
    produced `0` rows. The raw prefilter passed only `6 / 1281` decisions, but
    the final scored slate omitted the bad red/no-win candidates;
  - all-legal MPS smoke with the same exclusion also produced `0` rows, for the
    same reason;
  - turning off forced-lane-negative exclusion fixed the source shape:

| Shard | Seed | Rows | Rounds | Raw tactical pass | Proposal states | Above threshold | Bad red/no-win | Safe lane-preserving alts | Safe source-agreeing alts |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `shard006_noexclude_mps_smoke` | `20261708` | `2` | `15` | `3 / 458` | `3` | `2` | `3` | `5` | `5` |
| `shard007_noexclude_mps` | `20261709` | `4` | `125` | `18 / 4009` | `18` | `5` | `7` | `10` | `8` |

- Interpretation:
  - yes, the Strawberry/ReST/GRPO/expert-iteration idea applies directly, and
    this repo has already tried several versions of it;
  - the reason it has not solved survival yet is not that the idea is wrong.
    The currently useful winners/losers are sparse, source-sensitive, and
    easy to misgeneralize;
  - the immediate blocker was also mechanical: the candidate generator was
    allowed to exclude the very bad-red/no-win actions we need as hard
    negatives, so the verifier had too few true same-state contrasts;
  - Run971 restores productive hard-negative mining. This is training data,
    not a model candidate.
- Decision:
  - do not promote, install, live-screen, or distill from Run971 directly;
  - keep collecting several independent no-exclude hard-negative sources;
  - next training step should be source-held-out proposal verification with
    these Run970/971 sources in both train and holdout, then only if that
    passes consider a small policy-level best-of-N/RFT nudge.
- Verification:
  - `.venv/bin/python -m py_compile quantum_cat_live_substitution_replay.py`
    passed before the new shard collection;
  - `bad_red_safe_any_shard006_noexclude_mps_smoke` wrote `2` rows;
  - `bad_red_safe_any_shard007_noexclude_mps` wrote `4` rows.

### Run972 - explicit bad-red/no-win negatives help the named mistake, not the broader held-out candidate-any failure

- Date: `2026-06-15`.
- Goal:
  - continue Run971 by collecting more independent no-exclude hard-negative
    sources and testing whether a source-held-out proposal verifier can learn
    the user's red-switch rule: if the bot leaves the led color for red, red
    should usually win the trick; red lane burns that do not win should be
    rejected when lane-preserving alternatives exist.
- Data collection:
  - added two more 5p no-exclude MPS shards with the same Run971 collector

    `az_runs/run899_balanced_table_liveness_calibrated_20260614/holdout_cal_test_model.pt`;

    `2` rows from `125` rounds, `13 / 4000` raw tactical passes, `4` scored
    bad-red/no-win candidates, `5` safe lane-preserving alternatives;
  - `bad_red_safe_any_shard009_noexclude_mps.npz`, seed `20261711`:
    `2` rows from `125` rounds, `10 / 4034` raw tactical passes, `10` scored
    bad-red/no-win candidates, `4` safe lane-preserving alternatives.
- Code change:
  - `quantum_cat_proposal_veto_trainer.py` now has default-off
    `--bad-red-no-win-negative` and `--bad-red-no-win-penalty`;
  - scored-candidate views preserve public tactical flags
    `is_red_switch`, `switches_off_led`, `lost_led_token`, `would_win_now`,
    and `responsible_red_win_switch`;
  - when enabled, red switch + led-token loss + no current trick win is an
    explicit rejection condition and can receive extra group-relative reward
    penalty;
  - reports now count `bad_red_no_win_negative` in summaries, top-1 selections,
    and threshold approvals.
- Training setup:
  - base sources:
    the six strict repeated red/follow positive sources from Runs952-953 plus
    four live false-positive negative sources from Runs954-955;
  - hard held-out family:
    Run970 shard000 plus Run971/972 no-exclude shards006/007/008/009,
    installed as source indices `10-14`;
  - all screens used 5p source-held-out folds over the hard family, DeepSet,
    `scored_candidates`, `bce_listwise`, `group_relative_soft`, and
    `scalar_action_flags_win_aux_slate_state_round_history_context`.

| Variant | Held-out folds passed | Top-1 candidate-any total | Top-1 bad-red/no-win total | Decision |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `unsafe` baseline, Run970-style unsafe-margin | `2 / 5` | `5` | not explicitly tracked | reject |
| stronger source-balanced unsafe | `1 / 5` | `6` | `0` | reject |
| explicit bad-red/no-win penalty | `0 / 5` | `5` | `0` | reject |
| high unsafe + bad-red penalty diagnostic on holdouts `10,12` | `0 / 2` | `4` | `0` | reject |

- Interpretation:
  - source diversity improved the evidence quality but did not make the
    proposal verifier source-stable;
  - the explicit bad-red/no-win hook works for the named tactical error:
    every enabled bad-red variant had `0` top-1 bad-red/no-win selections and
    `0.0` bad-red/no-win approval rate at its best thresholds;
  - however, the harder held-out sources still choose candidate-any actions
    top-1, especially source `10` and source `12`. Increasing generic unsafe
    penalties either left candidate-any top-1 in place or collapsed into very
    low approval counts;
  - therefore this is useful infrastructure, but not a model candidate and not
    a reason to live-screen.
- Decision:
  - do not promote, install, distill, or live-screen any Run972 verifier;
  - keep `--bad-red-no-win-negative` as the right explicit concept;
  - the next useful step is richer same-state labels for candidate-any
    alternatives, not another scalar penalty sweep. In particular, mine more
    states like sources `10` and `12` and train with direct candidate-any
    contrast targets that separate "safe because base is also doomed" from
    "safe and actually non-paradox."

### Run974 - full candidate/base features fix one hard candidate-any source and worsen another

- Date: `2026-06-15`.
- Goal:
  - test whether Run973 failed because the compact feature family hides
    rank/card identity needed to distinguish same-color candidate-any actions
    from same-color non-paradox alternatives.
- Training:
  - same sources as Run973;
  - held-out sources:
    `10` and `12`, the old hard candidate-any failures;
  - same `bce_listwise`/bad-red/unsafe recipe as the Run973 augmented verifier;
  - feature mode changed to `full`, so the verifier sees the full candidate and
    base feature vectors plus their difference.

| Holdout | Gate | Top-1 candidate-any | Top-1 approved | Top-1 mean reward | Oracle reward |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `10` | fail | `5 / 5` | `0 / 5` | `-25.854573` | `1.196376` |
| `12` | fail | `0 / 4` | `2 / 4` | `0.981205` | `0.981820` |

- Interpretation:
  - representation matters: full features essentially solved holdout `12`'s
    ranking problem, matching the oracle reward and eliminating candidate-any
    top-1;
  - source `10` became worse, selecting candidate-any top-1 in every group.
    This source is probably a different rank/liquidity failure shape, not just
    missing rank features;
  - full features are promising evidence for the next architecture, but not a
    deployable verifier.
- Decision:
  - do not promote, install, distill, or live-screen Run974;
  - next useful step is source-10-focused error analysis and either:
    a rank/liquidity feature family that keeps full rank/card information
    without overfitting source rank, or a source-10-like data miner that
    produces more same-lane candidate-any versus non-paradox contrasts.

    at least `8` scored candidates) were too sparse:
    - shard001: `0 / 65` evaluated proposals accepted;
    - shard002: `0 / 65` evaluated proposals accepted.
  - near-density thresholds (`>=65%` candidate-any, `<=30%` approved/no-any,
    at least `6` scored candidates) were collectable:
    - shard003: `4 / 70` evaluated proposals accepted;
    - shard004: `4 / 65` evaluated proposals accepted.
  - with Run981's `2` strict rows, the training fork had `10` density rows.
- Training:

    `group_relative_soft`, unsafe margin `2.0`, unsafe weight `3.0`,
    `clean_safe` positives;

  - near-density collection works and produces the intended high-risk/sparse
    approved slates;
  - source-balanced training did not help transfer. It regressed hard source
    `10` versus Run978 (`4 / 5` candidate-any instead of `3 / 5`) while keeping
    source `12` clean;

- Interpretation:
  - the density contrast loss is real: training density contrast loss drops
    substantially in every enabled run;
  - unscoped contrast can improve one source-10-facing number, but it leaks
    damage into older source families, especially source `12`;
  - source scoping fixes the obvious source-12 top-1 contamination, but with
    only `10` density groups / `98` approved-vs-candidate-any pairs, it does
    not move the source-10 frontier enough;
  - this is closely related to best-of-rollouts / expert iteration: the next
    version should generate multiple full continuations from a state, score the
    resulting trajectories, and train listwise/pairwise preferences between
    successful and failing branches instead of relying on tiny same-slate
    density positives.

  - reject Runs984-988; no promotion, install, distill, or live-screen;
  - keep the default-off density contrast and source-filter hooks as
    infrastructure;
  - next best step is a ReST/expert-iteration-style trajectory generator:
    sample several continuations per hard state, rank them by no-paradox table
    survival plus score, then make the first actions from better continuations
    more likely and the first actions from collapse continuations less likely.

### Run990 - scaled best-of-rollouts banks validate the LLM-style policy-improvement path

- Date: `2026-06-15`.
- Goal:
  - answer whether the project can use the modern LLM-style loop the user
    described: sample multiple legal continuations, rank the resulting
    trajectories, and make the better first actions more likely;
  - distinguish that from promotion: this run validates the data/training path,
    not a new champion.
- Research framing:
  - this is the Cat-in-the-Box analogue of rejection-sampling fine-tuning /
    reward-ranked self-training / expert iteration:
    generate candidates from the current policy, score them with a verifier or
    rollout outcome, then train the fast policy toward the selected better
    action distribution;
  - locally, Runs946-947 already tried the tiny 5p version: Run946 nudged
    better actions upward and Run947 made repeat-validated better actions the
    top policy target. Both moved offline policy alignment, but the bank was
    too small and narrow to improve live same-policy survival.
- Data recipe:
  - generator:
    `quantum_cat_best_of_rollouts_replay.py`;
  - play-phase only, non-red led contrast only, require red-switch legal,
    require survival contrast, require changed policy target;
  - `2` rollouts per candidate action;
  - `5` max candidate actions, `3` policy-top actions;
  - target temperature `0.20`, top-score gap `2.0`.

|---:|---|---:|---:|---|---|

- Interpretation:
  - the expert-iteration loop is real: the policy stack can learn the
    rollout-selected first actions from small banks, especially in 4p/5p;
  - the learned offline target alignment still does not produce a deployable
    survival improvement. All probes are far above the `<40%` same-policy
    paradox target;
  - 4p exposes a different failure mode from 3p/5p: it almost never sloughs
    when the led color is legally available, yet still paradoxes heavily, so
    the next 4p data needs late forced-exit allocation, not just early
    led-preservation;
  - 3p and 5p still need stronger switch discipline. When switching, they do
    not choose red often enough, especially 3p (`69.92%` when red is legal)
    and 5p (`48.00%` overall).
- Decision:
  - reject Run991 checkpoints for promotion;
  - keep the banks, checkpoints, and gates as evidence that the pipeline
    transfers offline but needs much larger and better-balanced data;
  - next run should scale held-out best-of-rollouts banks by at least an order
    of magnitude, explicitly include red-when-switching and late forced-exit
    coverage, and use held-out target validation before full m200/m600 gates.

    ranking loss `0.5`;
  - no value/paradox/action-value loss in this pass, to isolate whether
    best-of-rollouts policy imitation improves live behavior.

- Interpretation:
  - strict best-of-rollouts is the first LLM-style policy-improvement pass
    that produced a large live survival movement in the right direction:
    compared with the earlier Run991 reduced screen, 3p improved
    `61.67% -> 42.78%`, 4p improved `76.67% -> 68.75%`, and 5p improved
    `77.67% -> 58.33%`;
  - still no promotion: none of the candidates clears the strict `<40%`
    same-policy paradox target, and 3p's `42.78%` is too close/noisy to
    install as champion;
  - 3p now mostly satisfies the user-requested red-switch rule when red is
    legal (`92.55%`), so the remaining 3p work is likely more data volume and
    late forced-exit coverage, not merely "choose red more";
  - 4p/5p still need stronger table-size-specific coverage. 4p follows led
    reasonably often but has weak red choice when red is legal; 5p chooses red
    when legal but often reaches states where red is not legal and non-red
    switches lose the trick.
- Decision:
  - reject all strict-bank Run991 candidates for promotion;
  - keep this as positive evidence for the best-of-rollouts direction;
  - next highest-value run is a much larger 3p strict bank first, with held-out
    validation and late forced-exit contrast, because 3p is now close enough to
    the `<40%` gate to justify a focused scale-up before broad 4p/5p spending.

### Run993 - 10x 3p strict best-of-rollouts scale-up, no promotion

  rows (`480` train and `144` validation), but the rollout teacher branched
  from the simulator's exact state and therefore read the opponents' private
  hands. The strengthened audit reports `0 / 624` information-safe rows. This
  bank is rejected as promotion evidence even though its source groups do not
  overlap.
- A second source-integrity bug also affected the nominal shield lane: a
  `liveness_shield?...` query string was passed through as an unrecognized bot
  mode and silently fell back to raw policy. The failure miner now parses and
  validates selector queries once up front and fails closed on unknown modes.
- Included `96` explicit late forced-exit contrast rows at tricks 5-7 (`72`
  train, `24` validation), rather than relying on incidental late-game states.

### Run994 - information-state repair exposes base-protection and trick-skew gaps

- Repaired best-of-rollouts generation so every candidate action is evaluated
  on actor-information-state resamples, with the same sampled worlds and
  continuation seeds shared across candidate actions. Observation and legal
  action equality are checked after every resample, and generation fails
  closed instead of falling back to the true deal.
- Built another `624`-row, source-disjoint bank (`480 / 144`) with `96`
  explicit trick-5--7 rows. All `624` rows passed the information-safety
  audit.
- The stronger audit then found two additional blockers:
  - only `245 / 624` rows beat the source action by at least `0.5` paired
    any-paradox rate, so the teacher still suffered sampled-action winner's
    curse;
  - the broad generators kept the first three decisions chronologically,
    leaving the bank concentrated at trick 0 and missing tricks 1--4 in both
    splits.
- Candidate A failed at `175 / 360 = 48.61%`. Candidate B also regressed in
  matched-seed screens (`46.67%` at step 20 and `48.89%` at step 40).
- Added paired base-action protection to both offline generation and the live
  information-state root selector. On the same tiny 12-match root-selector
  probe, the unprotected selector scored `25 / 36 = 69.44%`; requiring a
  `0.5` sampled any-paradox improvement reduced it to `14 / 36 = 38.89%`.
  The latter upper CI was `54.81%`, so it is directional evidence only.
- Rejected Run994 for training/promotion and changed broad decision sampling to
  seeded uniform sampling across each completed round.

### Run997 - proposal-aligned transfer audit finds and repairs any-player risk-target mismatch

- Converted the audited Run996 correction/base-keep banks into explicit
  candidate-vs-incumbent calibration pairs. The converter preserves source
  groups, replay targets, audit margins, and deployable feature provenance.
- Fixed a proposal-miner label bug: rejected rows had been exporting the
  incumbent as both sides of the calibration pair. Rejected rows now preserve
  the actual live proposed action as the candidate while retaining the
  incumbent as the deployment target.
- Added fail-closed calibration checks for explicit source disjointness and a
  common threshold that must pass every validation replay independently.
- The first proposal-aligned audit, using the historical acting-player risk
  target, showed severe distribution shift:
  - four train shards: `128` balanced rows, `22` POSITIVE and `106` hard
    non-positive proposals;
  - two held-out sources: `48` rows, `13` POSITIVE and `35` non-positive;
  - the original improve model assigned essentially `1.0` improve/safe
    probabilities to these proposals despite the low true-positive rate;
  - hand-engineered calibration MLPs, game-context variants, and frozen
    action-risk heads did not find a common source-disjoint precision gate.
- An information-safe online rollout selector was also rejected. On a fresh
  12-match late-trick screen it reached `16 / 36 = 44.44%`, 95% CI
  `[28.21%, 60.68%]`, versus the incumbent's `18 / 36 = 50.00%`, while taking
  `435.445` seconds. It remained above the strict threshold and was too slow
  to scale.
- Found a real objective mismatch in the expensive label path:
  - round rollouts could honor `counterfactual_action_paradox_scope=any`, but
    full-match proposal audits always returned only the acting player's
    paradox count;
  - this contradicted the primary homogeneous any-player paradox-rate gate;
  - full-match audits now count rounds with any paradox when scope is `any`,
    retain acting-player counts for explicit compatibility, default proposal
    mining to `any`, and embed the scope inside replay metadata.
- Added deployment-aligned risk-head validation metrics. Snapshot selection can
  now use within-state low-risk top-1/regret/correlation, with strict-contrast
  metrics that exclude equal-risk ties. This exposed why global Brier/correlation
  had looked healthier than the actual candidate-vs-incumbent decision.
- Regenerated corrected any-player proposal data:
  - train: `128` rows from four independent sources, exactly `16` per trick
    `0-7`, with `18` POSITIVE, `29` NEAR_POSITIVE, and `81` NEGATIVE;
  - validation: `16` rows from a fifth source, exactly `2` per trick, with
    `3` POSITIVE, `6` NEAR_POSITIVE, and `7` NEGATIVE;
  - source overlap: zero; every NPZ reports
    `counterfactual_action_paradox_scope=any`.
- Corrected-model results still fail:
  - the frozen action-risk head's best strict held-out ordering was only
    `5 / 10`, so it was rejected before live evaluation;
  - the richer deployable calibration MLP's best held-out threshold approved
    one row, but that row had a worse any-player paradox delta; no threshold
    met the minimum two true safe overrides, so `offline_gate_pass=false`.
- Decision:
  - retain the scope repair, replay provenance, and strict-contrast validation
    infrastructure;
  - reject all Run997 policy/verifier candidates and leave the incumbent
    unchanged;
  - do not spend on independent 600-match gates or 4p/5p training yet;
  - the binding ML issue is now explicit: the proposal model is badly
    overconfident out of distribution, and neither the shared action
    representation nor the current deployable pair features generalize the
    trajectory audit boundary.

### Run998 - top-k proposal expansion still does not generalize

- Expanded live proposal audits from the top proposal only to the top three
  scored candidates. This fixed a real data-loss bug: lower-ranked candidates
  can be true corrections even when the primary proposal is unsafe.
- Built four train sources with `128` state rows and two held-out sources with
  `32` state rows. Candidate expansion produced `432` unique train pairs
  (`40` POSITIVE) and `150` held-out pairs (`13` POSITIVE), with zero source
  overlap.
- Fixed both calibration trainers so top-k states expand to candidate-level
  examples while retaining one state group, preventing candidate leakage
  across splits. The listwise path now also requires one threshold to pass
  every input source independently.
- Results:
  - a pairwise verifier's best aggregate threshold reached only `43.5%`
    precision; the two held-out sources peaked at `50.0%` and `44.4%` and had
    no shared passing threshold;
  - the listwise verifier's best aggregate threshold reached `55.56%`, but one
    held-out source found zero true positives, so no shared gate existed;
  - direct policy-head and policy-action-stack fits either failed to recall
    positives or began changing audited base-keep rows before recall became
    source-stable.
- Decision: reject every Run998 checkpoint/verifier. Top-k preservation is
  retained as infrastructure, but the proposal model is not told which
  externally generated candidate it is judging and its boundary remains
  source-unstable.

### Run999 - repeated audits invalidate the apparent proposal positives

- Found a more fundamental supervision issue: proposal labels used only two
  full-match continuations per action. A single changed paradox outcome moves
  the estimated risk by `0.5`, so pooled two-rollout positives can be sampling
  artifacts.
- Added fail-closed stability audits to the proposal miner:
  - independent audit passes with disjoint seed ranges;
  - per-candidate score-margin and any-player paradox-delta vectors;
  - configurable positive-sign and safe-risk repeatability requirements;
  - aggregate positives that fail repeatability hard-target the incumbent.
- Two independent, trick-balanced sources each audited `16` states with top-3
  candidates, three passes, and two full-match rollouts per pass. Across `76`
  candidate evaluations, zero candidates were stable positives. Eleven looked

### Run1002 - deployable public sequence memory is clean but does not generalize

- Replaced the existing training-only "round context" idea with an exact,
  deployable public-history contract. The normal observation records the
  current board/tokens but not the order of prior public plays; Run1002 adds a
  `32`-value sequence summary plus `11` candidate/history interactions. It
  reads only completed tricks and already exposed cards, never hands or
  face-down discards.
- One shared encoder now serves all three paths:
  - strict replay collection writes `public_history` metadata;
  - the ActionSetTransformer trainer requires the exact version/schema and
    refuses missing rows;
  - live full-match inference reconstructs the same features from game state
    and accepts only the exact deployable schema. The old sparse labeled-row
    reconstruction remains explicitly legacy/offline-only.
- Deterministically reconstructed the clean Run996 bank from its source
  checkpoint, seed, match, round, and decision provenance. Every one of the
  `535` rows (`416 + 41` train, `62 + 16` held out) matched its stored
  observation exactly, plus legal set, player, trick, and source action,
  before history metadata was admitted.
- Found and repaired three selector-supervision bugs during the audit:
  - explicit metadata sidecars were silently discarded whenever the base
    action came from the policy-context checkpoint;
  - fresh-audit-rejected base keeps inherited optimistic selection-world
    auxiliary labels and could therefore teach the rejected override;
  - the set trainer had no target mode that honored the replay's explicit
    action, so a hard base-keep target could be replaced by an auxiliary
    best-action target.
  Explicit sidecars are now retained, audit-rejected alternatives are shaped
  conservatively, and `target_mode=replay_action` honors the audited target.
- Source-held-out result, same seed and architecture:
  - corrected stateless baseline: best validation precision `70.69%`
    (`41 / 58` positive selections), no eligible `>=85%` precision gate;
  - public-history model: best validation precision `68.00%` (`34 / 50`),
    also no eligible gate;
  - the history fork therefore regressed the already-failing baseline and was
    rejected before any performance screen.
- A fail-closed one-match deployment smoke used an impossible override margin
  (`1000`) and successfully scored `164` live candidates across `61`
  considered decisions with the public-history schema. This proves feature
  parity/wiring only; the `1 / 3` paradox-round result is not performance
  evidence.
- Decision:
  - retain the public-history encoder, deterministic enrichment verifier, and
    supervision repairs;
  - reject both Run1002 selectors and do not run 600-round promotion gates;
  - sequence order alone is not the missing discriminator on the current
    sparse first-action bank. The remaining credible fork needs denser
    multi-decision trajectory targets or a much higher-precision audit, not
    another classifier over the same `535` endpoints.

### Run1003 - chained trajectory supervision is valid but too sparse to transfer

- Replaced frozen-endpoint mining with an online chained collector. Every
  eligible decision is evaluated on common actor-information-state worlds;
  an override is applied to the actual trajectory only after three disjoint
  fresh audit passes each clear the configured any-player paradox-improvement
  floor. Later examples therefore include states induced by earlier audited
  corrections rather than only incumbent trajectories.
- The first strict audit found a real target-integrity bug: selection-time soft
  targets could retain probability on tied or near-best actions that had never
  passed the independent audit. Correction targets are now hard one-hot on the
  single audited action. The V2 contract also stores an exact public play trace,
  correction ancestry, explicit incumbent action, collector configuration, and
  every selection/audit seed; empty positive shards cannot leave stale replay
  files behind.
- The full V2 bank passed the strict replay audit:
  - `2,736` evaluated decisions from `16` source groups and `162` trajectories;
  - `24` audited corrections and `261` selection-positive audit rejections
    hard-targeted to the incumbent;
  - positive trick coverage `{0: 4, 1: 1, 4: 8, 5: 4, 6: 5, 7: 2}`;
  - `141` decisions were evaluated after a prior correction and `13` emitted
    labels were downstream of one;
  - no audit errors, duplicate seed pairs, duplicate seed values, trace
    mismatches, target mismatches, or correction-ancestry mismatches.
- Whole-source training/validation split:
  - train: `14` corrections plus `148` audited base keeps;
  - held out: `10` corrections plus `113` audited base keeps, including early,
    late, trick-7, and intentionally empty-positive source groups;
  - source overlap: zero.
- Direct action-set learning failed across six independent fits. Three
  public-history/summary models (`2,421` input features) and three
  raw-summary models (`2,497` features) memorized the training positives, but
  every model's best held-out threshold had `0%` correction precision. The
  validation positive head generally assigned near-zero probability to the
  true held-out corrections.
- Policy-head transfer also failed across three independent seeds. The best
  loaded-replay snapshots hit `0 / 10` held-out corrections; their only
  changes were false overrides of audited base keeps. At the most favorable
  screened thresholds they produced `1-2` false overrides, `0%` precision,
  `0%` recall, and `98.23-99.12%` base-keep rates. The frozen incumbent
  correctly abstained on all `113` base keeps but also recalled `0 / 10`
  corrections.
- One operational mistake was contained: the policy-head commands omitted
  `--iterations 0` and continued into default self-play after loaded-replay
  training. Only the `checkpoint_0000_loaded_replay_best.pt` artifacts saved
  before that continuation were audited; all later checkpoints and inherited
  metrics were excluded. Future loaded-only commands must set
  `--iterations 0`.
- Decision:
  - retain the chained collector, V2 replay contract, hard audited targets,
    strict replay auditor, and class-aware checkpoint auditor;
  - reject all Run1003 selectors and policy-head checkpoints;
  - do not run a 600-round performance gate: no candidate passed the offline
    source-disjoint precision/recall screen;
  - the immediate blocker is sample-efficient, source-invariant credit
    assignment. The accepted correction rate is only `24 / 2,736 = 0.88%`,
    leaving `14` train positives for a `2.4k+`-feature selector. The next bank
    must increase independent-audit precision and accepted correction density,
    then screen a much lower-capacity public-feature model before another live
    candidate.

### Run1004 - exact paired evidence and low-capacity correction learning

- The first low-capacity screens were run on the clean Run1003 chained bank:
  three pair-only action-set fits, three compact-action-delta fits, and three
  linear fits for each of the full and compact pair representations. All were
  rejected before live play. None cleared the source-disjoint `>=85%`
  correction-precision gate; the best validation thresholds continued to
  select held-out base keeps as false overrides, usually at `0%` correction
  precision.
- Added exact paired continuation evidence to the chained collector. Each
  audit pass now records saved, harmed, and tied any-player-paradox outcomes
  and can require a one-sided exact-binomial `p` ceiling. This is stricter than
  a mean-rate delta because a candidate cannot pass on an unpaired aggregate
  fluctuation.
- Three initial late-game source groups used:
  - tricks `4-7` only;
  - `16` information-state worlds x `2` continuations per action in each of
    three independent audit passes;
  - minimum per-pass any-paradox improvement `0.125`;
  - per-pass exact paired one-sided binomial `p <= 0.1`;
  - hard one-hot target on the independently audited action.
- Result: `3` accepted corrections and `11` audited base keeps from `864`
  evaluated decisions. The three corrections cover tricks `4`, `5`, and `7`.
  Every accepted correction passed all three independent audit passes; the
  weakest accepted per-pass exact `p` was `0.0546875`.
- Immediate next step: collect enough additional independent source groups to
  support a whole-source train/validation split, then refit only the compact
  linear pair model. A live screen remains forbidden unless the held-out
  correction precision/recall gate passes.
- Current artifacts:
  - `az_runs/run1004_3p_high_precision_chained_20260721/hpp_late_0_summary.json`;
  - `az_runs/run1004_3p_high_precision_chained_20260721/hpp_late_1_summary.json`;
  - `az_runs/run1004_3p_high_precision_chained_20260721/hpp_late_2_summary.json`.
- The exact-p bank was then scaled from the three initial sources to fifteen
  independent source groups. Selection used four information-state worlds and
  one continuation per action to find candidates, while every accepted target
  still had to pass three fresh audits of `16` information-state worlds x `2`
  paired continuations per action, minimum any-player-paradox improvement
  `0.125` in every pass, and one-sided exact-binomial `p <= 0.1` in every pass.
  Six source groups additionally required explicit forced-paradox contrast at
  tricks `5-7`.
- Final strict-bank result: `63` accepted corrections and `285` audit-rejected
  base keeps from `4,320` evaluated decisions across `15` source groups and
  `264` trajectories. Correction coverage is trick `4: 1`, trick `5: 15`,
  trick `6: 37`, and trick `7: 10`. The replay audit passed with no errors, no
  duplicated audit seed pairs, and no duplicated audit seed values.
- Whole-source development validation reserved `hpp50_late_5` and
  `hpp50_forced_8`: `10` corrections plus `37` base keeps, including forced
  examples at tricks `5-7`. Two newer forced sources, `hpp50_forced_12` and
  `hpp50_forced_13`, were sealed as a never-trained final holdout (`10`
  corrections plus `40` base keeps). Because no development candidate passed,
  the final holdout was not opened for model selection or reported as a gate.
- Compact linear pair fits improved over the Run1003 bank but failed the
  development gate. Before the final forced wave, their best high-precision
  slice selected `5 / 7` true corrections (`71.43%`), and their best slice at
  the required eight-override floor was at most `5 / 9` (`55.56%`).
- Tiny regularized action-set models, raw information-legal observation
  variants, a wider probability/margin calibration sweep, and one bounded
  six-model ensemble also failed. The strongest eight-override development
  result was `6 / 8 = 75%` correction precision; conservative settings could
  reach `5 / 6 = 83.33%` or `7 / 7 = 100%`, but not the required recall. No
  configuration reached the `>= 8` overrides and `>= 85%` precision contract.
- Decision:
  - retain the exact paired collector, the strict replay auditor, the
    high-precision `63 / 285` bank, and the sealed final holdout;
  - reject every Run1004 selector checkpoint and do not run a live or 600-round
    promotion screen;
  - treat information-legal teacher-to-policy distillation as the current
    blocker. The audit teacher reliably finds corrections, but existing
    deployable features/models cannot yet distinguish them from independently
    rejected lookalikes at both high precision and useful recall;
  - the next justified line is a genuinely different representation/objective
    or an inference-time information-state search shield, not more seed or
    threshold tuning on the same development groups.

### Run1005 - inference-time exact-audited information-state search

- Run1004 closed the learned-selector route without a live candidate, so this
  run moved to the materially different fallback: perform the information-safe
  search at inference time and fail closed unless fresh evidence supports the
  override.
- Hardened `:root_rollout` in `quantum_cat_full_match_elo.py`:
  - common-seed action scoring now retains the paired paradox outcome vector;
  - `--root-rollout-audit-passes` requires multiple independently resampled
    audit passes;
  - `--root-rollout-max-audit-paired-binomial-p` requires a one-sided exact
    saved-vs-harmed paired-outcome p-value in every pass;
  - missing/misaligned outcome vectors, failed belief resampling, a weak mean
    improvement, a weak exact p-value, or any failed pass all keep the raw
    policy action;
  - per-bot query overrides and decision statistics expose the new contract.
- A 10-match functional smoke at tricks `5-7` used two audit passes of `8`
  information-state worlds x one paired continuation, mean audit improvement
  `>= 0.125`, and exact `p <= 0.1`. It considered `20` proposed overrides and
  blocked all `20`; one first pass cleared before its later pass failed. This
  is correct fail-closed branch coverage, not a performance result or a model
  promotion.
- Validation: the full training suite passed `184` tests, including exact-p
  acceptance, weak-p rejection, missing-outcome rejection, and per-bot option
  parsing. The evaluator smoke completed with zero belief-sampling failures.

### Run1006 - independent-world inference and strict 3p scale-up

- Corrected a statistical validity bug in the Run1004/Run1005 audit contract.
  The old `16` information-state worlds x `2` deterministic continuations
  flattened all `32` outcomes into the exact sign test. Because Quantum Cat
  has no post-deal chance and the continuation policy is deterministic, the
  two continuations from each world were duplicates, not independent samples.
  Recomputing the Run1004 bank at the information-state-world level retains
  only `36 / 63` corrections; `27` had passed only through duplicated
  evidence. The surviving corrections cover trick `5: 7`, trick `6: 19`, and
  trick `7: 10`; the sole trick-4 row does not survive.
- Bumped the chained replay contract to
  `chained_best_of_rollouts_v3`. Exact evidence now compares one paired mean
  per independently sampled information-state world, while continuation
  outcomes remain diagnostic only. The root-rollout evaluator uses the same
  world-level inference unit. Added explicit audit error reasons, normalized
  derived NumPy seeds into the valid 32-bit range, and made the replay auditor
  fail on malformed world-level evidence.
- Added canonical source-group split validation to the action-set trainer and
  carried source-group identity through the legal-set selector. A fit now
  fails if any collector source group crosses train/development boundaries.
- Recollected the strict bank from scratch with:
  - `4,320` evaluated decisions across `15` disjoint source groups;
  - `9` late-game groups plus `6` groups requiring forced-paradox contrast;
  - three fresh audit passes of `32` independent information-state worlds x
    one continuation, minimum per-pass any-player-paradox improvement `0.125`,
    and one-sided exact sign-test `p <= 0.1` in every pass;
  - `52` accepted corrections, `313` independently audited base keeps, and
    `287` trajectories;
  - correction coverage trick `5: 16`, trick `6: 29`, trick `7: 7`;
  - no duplicate audit seed pairs or values and no audit errors.
- Whole-source development validation reserved `late_4` and `forced_4`, with
  `15` corrections and `43` base keeps covering tricks `5-7` and forced-exit
  examples. The remaining groups provide `37` corrections and `270` base
  keeps for training. Two transformer fits and one compact linear fit all
  failed the deployment gate: the best transformer produced only four
  perfect-precision overrides, while the linear model's required eight-plus
  slice reached only `7 / 16 = 43.75%` precision. No learned selector was
  promoted or live-screened.
- Corrected inference-time root-rollout screens used `32` independent audit
  worlds x one continuation, three fresh passes, per-pass improvement
  `>= 0.125`, and exact `p <= 0.1`. On seed `2026083001`, the raw checkpoint
  had `76 / 180 = 42.22%` paradox rounds. Strict screens improved as follows:
  - four-world proposal, tricks `5-7`: `72 / 180 = 40.00%`;
  - eight-world proposal, tricks `5-7`: `71 / 180 = 39.44%`;
  - eight-world proposal, tricks `4-7`: `70 / 180 = 38.89%`;
  - proposal margin `0.25`, tricks `4-7`: `69 / 180 = 38.33%`;
  - all legal actions, tricks `4-7`: `68 / 180 = 37.78%`;
  - tricks `3-7`: `63 / 180 = 35.00%`.
- A harder independent seed, `2026083002`, had `91 / 180 = 50.56%` raw
  paradox rounds. The trick-4 variants reached `76-77 / 180`, and the trick-3
  variant reached `77 / 180 = 42.78%`. The paired hand-round trace proves the
  effect is real despite the hard aggregate distribution: the all-action
  trick-4 shield saved `14` raw-policy paradox rounds and harmed `0`
  (`p = 0.000061`), while trick 3 saved `16` and harmed `2`
  (`p = 0.000656`). Trick-3 results pool to `140 / 360 = 38.89%`, versus
  `167 / 360 = 46.39%` raw.
- Tightened the homogeneous promotion gate itself:
  - confidence intervals now use the Wilson score method;
  - `passed` now requires the any-paradox CI95 upper bound below the declared
    threshold instead of merely a passing point estimate;
  - compact, stably ordered per-hand paradox outcomes are retained for
    same-deal paired comparisons.
  At `1,800` hand rounds, the `40%` gate permits at most `679` paradox rounds
  (`37.72%` point estimate). Extending the same shield through tricks `2-7`
  produced `63 / 180 = 35.00%` and `72 / 180 = 40.00%` on the two seeds,
  pooling to `135 / 360 = 37.50%`. Against their same-deal raw controls, the
  shield saved/harmed `14 / 1` and `19 / 0` hand rounds respectively, while
  improving average player match score on both seeds. A third seed reached
  only `72 / 180 = 40.00%` against `77 / 180 = 42.78%` raw, so the three-seed
  pool was `207 / 540 = 38.33%`, above the large-gate entry bar.
- A final full-play screen on the third seed reached `69 / 180 = 38.33%`, but
  recorded no accepted overrides on tricks `0-1`. Merely evaluating those
  no-op states had changed later actions because root search consumed the
  process-global NumPy stream. That made later search decisions depend on how
  many earlier states happened to be inspected. The evaluator now seeds a
  private search RNG from a SHA-256 digest of the acting player's observation,

#### Formal independent-gate hardening

- The formal promotion runner now requires at least three independent gates
  with at least `600` matches apiece. It derives a unique gameplay and led-audit
  seed for each gate and records both in the per-gate summary.
- A new aggregate manifest fails closed unless every expected gate is present,
  uses the same checkpoint and selector contracts, has distinct gameplay and
  led-audit seeds, keeps player count and the gameplay/led-audit selector
  identical, declares the exact `40%` threshold, and independently reports a
  Wilson CI95 upper bound below that threshold. Its pooled interval is
  explicitly informational and cannot conceal a failed individual gate.
- Focused validation passed `11` tests covering the aggregate gate, telemetry,
  and web logger. Shell validation also confirmed that the formal runner exits
  `2` before evaluation when configured with only two gates, `599` matches, or
  a relaxed `50%` threshold, and when its led-audit selector differs from the
  gameplay selector.

  inference units, exact world counts, improvement margins, and paired

  phase, search seed, selection evidence, and the audit contract in durable

- On fresh hard seed `2026084003`, raw policy produced

  exact same mean score. It audited `425` proposals versus `179`, accepted
  `15` overrides versus `13`, and took `1420.0s` versus `1193.0s`. Its two
  extra accepted overrides changed no survival or score outcome. Reject the
  lower proposal margin.
- The high audit volume exposed a replay-integrity bug: decision-stat list
  aggregation retained only the first `100` samples per alias, so the raw
  lower-margin artifact recorded only `12 / 15` accepted overrides. The
  replay converter now fails closed when recorded accepted rows do not exactly
  match the evaluator's accepted override count; it correctly rejects this
  incomplete replay while preserving the live screen as diagnostic evidence.

  bounding only rejected base-keep rows to `100` per alias. Future replay
  artifacts therefore remain size-bounded without losing positive rows.
- The valid `0.25` replay converted `179` rows (`13` corrections / `166` base
  keeps). The incomplete `0.125` replay was not emitted.

#### Human telemetry/Elo integrity follow-up

- Removed face-down discarded ranks from the web logger. Those ranks are
  available to the terminal simulator but were never public evidence; keeping
  them in a completed record violated the hidden-information-free telemetry
  contract. The validator now rejects `discardedRank(s)` keys in addition to
  hands and decks.
- Upgraded the telemetry report to schema V2:
  - Elo pools are separated by player count, so 3p/4p/5p evidence can no
    longer contaminate one rating ladder;
  - ratings can be tied to a frozen table-size-specific anchor file, and the
    anchor ratings never drift during online updates or bootstrapping;
  - graph connectivity is reported per participant, so a human cohort that
    never faced a frozen reference cannot be mislabeled as absolutely
    anchored;
  - the report computes an appearance-weighted human-cohort Elo and a joint
    bootstrap CI for every bot-minus-human Elo difference, so the eventual
    claim is evaluated directly rather than inferred from overlapping
    participant intervals;
  - the claim state remains `needs_100_human_matches` below the mission's
    minimum and remains diagnostic-only when any Core ML participant used an
    unverified live input contract.
- iOS bot telemetry identities now include the live input contract. A bundled
  checkpoint running through the fail-closed Swift fallback and the same
  checkpoint running through the verified `76/214` encoder are therefore
  different Elo competitors rather than silently merged observations.
- Frozen anchor configuration:
  `experiments/human_elo_anchor_pool.json`. Its 3p coordinate is the exact
  current champion SHA under the verified live-input contract; 2p/4p/5p use
  the native target heuristic as the `1000` coordinate. This defines a rating
  origin, not a human-performance result.

  per-pass improvement consistently from `0.125` to `0.0625`; the exact
  paired-binomial requirement remained `p <= 0.10` on every pass.
- Raw policy and the higher-power candidate both produced
  `13 / 30 = 43.33%` paradox rounds. The candidate made five accepted
  overrides, saving two same-deal rounds and harming two, while mean player
  score moved only `8.3667 -> 8.4667`. All `87` proposals were independently
  audited, `82` were blocked, and belief-sampling failures remained zero.
- Reject the higher-power recipe: more audit worlds did not create a
  directional survival improvement and the point estimate remains above the
  formal-gate entry bar.
- Artifacts: `az_runs/run1013_3p_audit_power_20260722/`.

### Run1014 - uniform information-state liveness estimates are unsafe

- Audited `120` trick-5-7 play states from `20` fresh 3p matches using `16`
  uniform information-state samples per state. The diagnostic compared the
  belief-selected table-liveness action with the exact hidden-state oracle;
  exact state is used only for evaluation, never for a deployable choice.
- Belief and exact-oracle best actions matched on `77 / 120 = 64.17%` states.
  Among all belief overrides, only `26 / 63 = 41.27%` matched the exact best
  action. Stability filtering retained `38` overrides but only `19 / 38`
  matched the exact best action and only `10 / 38 = 26.32%` were non-worse
  than the policy action under the exact diagnostic.
- Raising the belief margin did not repair safety: the non-worse rate was
  `42.11%` at margin `>=0.75` (`8 / 19`) and `50%` at margin `>=2.0`
  (`4 / 8`). Reject uniform belief liveness as a live selector and do not
  implement it in the app or evaluator.
- Artifact:
  `az_runs/run1014_3p_belief_table_liveness_20260722/infostate_m20_s16_max120_seed2026084301.json`.

### Run1032 - foundational search, belief, and validation-integrity audit

- Scope: independently audit the shared AlphaZero search, belief posterior,
  counterfactual world sampling, and source-disjoint replay validation before

  - one simulated depth-two trajectory backed up its intermediate node twice
    (`root=1`, `intermediate=2`, `terminal=1`), corrupting PUCT counts and
    every belief-MCTS teacher target;
  - the batched belief posterior assigned probability `0.163253` to the
    deterministic shared bid and `0.142502` to an impossible alternative,
    while the real scalar policy probabilities were exactly `1` and `0`;
  - a supposedly group-held-out split left an unlabeled row from the selected
    validation source inside training, and missing source metadata silently
    downgraded to a row split;
  - a failed information-state resample silently returned a clone of the
    actual fully observed state, leaking real opponent hands into training
    and teacher rollouts.
- Additional posterior and evaluation defects reproduced after the first fix:
  - an exactly impossible deterministic bid was floored to log-likelihood
    `-13.815511` instead of rejecting its hidden world;
  - the posterior's uniform exploration mixture put `25%` probability on a
    world already scored as logically impossible in a two-candidate audit;
  - when posterior scoring returned no likelihood, the old policy-weighted
    branch silently reverted to unverified uniform hidden worlds;
  - one real four-player deal on seed `2026103101` admitted only
    `10 / 1000 = 1%` bid-consistent uniform samples, so a fixed 128-candidate
    rejection budget could fail before finding a valid world;
  - explicit validation replay could reuse an identical training file or a
    different file produced by the same collector source;
  - action-conditioned inference evaluated the entire `1000`-action space
    even when the real position exposed just `21` legal actions.
- Existing baseline: `249` focused engine/model/evaluation regression tests
  passed before the new reproductions, confirming these defects were not
  protected by the prior suite.
- Fixes:
  - back up every visited search node exactly once;
  - honor deterministic shared discard/bid behavior in batched posterior
    likelihoods, reject bid-inconsistent worlds in both scalar and batched
    scorers, and keep uniform posterior exploration strictly within valid
    support;
  - expand rejection batches geometrically when public bid evidence is rare,
    while failing closed if no valid information-state world can be found;
  - never substitute the actual private simulator state for a failed belief
    resample;
  - hold out every row from selected collector sources and reject missing,
    incomplete, reused, or overlapping explicit validation provenance;
  - evaluate legal action-feature rows only for `action_mlp`, `action_attn`,
    and `action_setpool`, preserving the existing 1000-action public API and
    all policy/value/risk outputs on legal actions.
- Measured real-checkpoint inference: `21` legal actions out of `1000`;
  dense neural forward `3.5167 ms`, compact forward `0.4165 ms`, or `8.44x`
  faster, with zero legal-logit difference and maximum value difference
  `0.0000000298`.

## Run1035 - Official competitive placement replaces the table-wide paradox veto

- User-approved objective correction: the official rules penalize only the
  player who personally causes a paradox; opponents still score and can benefit
  from trapping a rival. Board Game Arena Elo compares official final match
  placements, not whether anybody at the table paradoxed. The historical
  `<40%` homogeneous any-player threshold originated as an internal 3p
  heuristic and is retired as a promotion requirement for every player count.
- Binding primary evidence: full base-game official total score and final-round
  tiebreak; exact frozen player-count-specific incumbent selector; every
  candidate seat on each common chance deal; Student-t confidence and p-values
  across independent deals, never across correlated seats/opponent comparisons.
  A 4p all-permutations schedule repeats the three identical incumbent aliases
  six times, so the new cyclic schedule runs exactly four unique seats/deal.
- Personal safety guard: candidate paradoxes / candidate hand-round
  opportunities versus incumbent paradoxes / incumbent seat-round
  opportunities. Block significant candidate-only regression and count actual
  trick reversals plus forfeited prediction bonuses. Opponent paradoxes and
  homogeneous table-wide paradox rates remain diagnostics, never vetoes.
- Evaluator changes: native `--schedule=cyclic`, competitive promotion summary,
  exact official placement, tie-aware BGA rank points, deal-clustered Student-t
  intervals, personal/opponent paradox rates, points lost, scored bid accuracy,
  adjacency bonuses, and compact diagnostic output. The existing homogeneous
  summary remains backward-compatible but has no formal decision authority.
- Operational changes: Mac and independent formal wrappers now freeze the
  correct raw 3p, Run730 public-liveness 4p, and Run600 q-policy 5p references;
  verify both checkpoint hashes and exact selector modes; require three
  independent gate seeds, at least 600 genuinely seat-rotated matches/gate,
  enough distinct deals, significant placement gain, score nonregression, and
  zero-tolerance significant personal-paradox regression.
- Competitive experiment 1, exact unchanged Run1034 teacher student:
  `12` independent common deals x `4` unique seats = `48` full
  competitive matches. Pairwise official placement `72W / 2T / 70L`,
  `50.69%`, approximately `+4.83 Elo`; mean rank points
